segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎯᏅ ᏝᎦ ᏙᏓᏛᏢᏃᎮᏟ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ, ᎯᏅ ᏥᎾᏅᏛᏁ ᏥᏚᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ Ꮎ ᎠᏭ ᏗᏓᏅᏕᎳᏆ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ. ᎡᎵᏭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏯᎾᏕᏠᏆ ᎢᏗᏬᏂᎲᎢ ᏃᎴ ᎾᏍᏊ ᏢᎮᏂᏴ ᎡᎵᏭ ᎯᎢ ᎢᏓᏓᏗᏬᏂ ᏍᏊ ᏍᏛᏌ ᏴᏍᏛᏛᏓᏍᏗ ᏍᎩ Ꮎ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏢᏅᏕᏍᏓ ᎯᏅ ᏛᏍᏛᏯᏛᏛᎮᏢᏂ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎤᏃᏪᎸ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏍᏊ ᏍᏛᏍᎬᏢᏍᏗ ᎢᏍᏓᏚᎵᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏥᏍᏓᏛᎾ. Ꮩ ᏕᏍᏓᏙ ᏳᏁᎩ ᎬᏗ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ Ꮕ ᎬᏗ?
segments.translation: We all are going to talk a little while, all Cherokee. The work that they’re doing here, they might learn something from this language. And at some point y’all might listen to this yourselves. There will always be room for that. I’m going to ask y’all some questions that are written here. But then again, if y’all want to hide something, y’all don’t have to say anything. What are your names in Cherokee and English?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: Henry Lee Sawney ᏓᏩᏙ ᏣᎳᎩᏅ ᎬᏗ ᎮᏂᎵ ᏓᏩᏙ.
segments.translation: Henry Lee Sawney, in Cherokee my name is He-Ni-Li.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎮᏂᎵ. ᏂᎯᎾ?
segments.translation: He-Ni-Li. And you?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏅ Jerry Cochran ᏙᎡ ᎨᎲ ᏤᏏᏭ ᎬᏬᎮᎰ.
segments.translation: Jerry Cochran, they also call me Tse-Si.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎭᏢᏂ ᏍᏛᏛᏏᏙᎸ?
segments.translation: Where did y’all grow up?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: SalemᎢᏛ ᏦᎩᎾᏛᏒ.
segments.translation: We grew up around Salem [Adair County, Oklahoma].

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: SalemᎢ yeah.
segments.translation: Salem, yeah.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏅᏃ ᏗᎦᎾᏗᏫᏒ ᏂᏙᎩᎾᏓᎵ Ꮟ ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ.
segments.translation: We live across the road from each other.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗᏓᏁ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎮ Ꮎ ᎠᏕᏗ ᏓᏕᏍᏗᏛᏏᏗᏒ?
segments.translation: What was it like back then when y’all were growing up?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎡᎳᏗ ᏛᎭ ᎨᎲ ᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎾᎦᎵᏍᎦ Ꮲ ᏰᎮ.
segments.translation: We were on foot, there wasn’t any electricity.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏝᎩ?
segments.translation: There wasn’t?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎲᎥ, ᏲᎮᏂ Ꮟ ᏱᏛᏢᏃᎲᎵ ᎨᎲ ᎪᎮᏂ ᏥᎩ Ꮲ ᏱᏛᎬᏴᏢᏃᎲᎵ ᏧᎾᏢᏃᎮᏗ ᏛᎾᎦᏎᏍᏛ ᏴᏫ.
segments.translation: No, but you could talk back then. Now you can’t talk ’cause everybody’s looking at their cellphone.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎲ ᏱᎾᏛᏁ ᏙᎲ? [gestures]
segments.translation: Oh, they would be doing this [gestures].

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏓᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏕᏗ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᏩᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᎠᏯ.
segments.translation: It was a good life, a long time ago.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏥᎩ ᏗᏁᏟᏙᏗ ᏚᏂᎾᎣ ᏴᏛᏂ Walmart ᏧᏂᎩᏓ. ᏂᎯᎾ ᏙᎤᏍᏗ ᏍᏗᎮ ᏗᏍᏓᏁᏟᏙᏗ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ?
segments.translation: Nowadays kids have things that they got from Walmart. What did you all have back then, growing up?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: Ꮎ blocks Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏛ ᎠᏓ board ᎤᎵᎦᎲᎸᏓ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏙᏥᏒᏙᏱᏙᎰ ᏗᎦᏚᎴᏂ ᏦᎩᏰᎸᎯ Ꮎ ᎴᏱᎩᏅ ᏙᏩᎴᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏪᏘ Ꮎ ᏙᏱ ᏗᏢ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏔᎷᎩᏍᎦ Ᏼ ᏯᏖᏂ ᏥᎦᏩᏙ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏯᏩᏛ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏯᏖᏂ ᎾᏅ ᏦᎳ ᎦᏢᏛᏅ ᏱᏣᏯᎸᏂ ᎥᎾ ᏱᏕᏣᏍᏈᏛᏂ ᎥᎾ boy ᎠᏯᏄᎵ ᎴᏱᎩ ᏲᏲ ᎨᎲ. Boy ᏳᏫᎳᏍᏛᏂ ᏍᎩᏂ ᏛᏨᎬᏛᏂᎵ Ꮫ ᎨᎲ. ᏅᏛᎭᏍ Ꮚ ᎦᏄᎸᎯ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᏚᏙᎥ ᎨᎲᏲ ᎣᏦᏎᎲ ᎠᏯ. ᏌᎪᏂᎨ ᎠᏥᎸᏍᎩ. ᏢᏴ ᏱᏗᎦᏗ [gestures] ᏱᏣᏰᎯᏏᏃ ᏗᎭᏄᎸᎯᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏚᏔᎾᎶᏭ ᎡᎵᏍᏓ. ᏍᎩᏛ ᏙᏨᏙᎩᏯᏍᏗᎰ ᎨᎲ ᏂᏙᎬᎳᎱᏢᏂ ᎮᏍᏕ ᎮᏂ ᎰᏩ ᏗᎳᎱᎶ ᏦᏨᎳᏑᏢᏍᎩ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ.
segments.translation: When we would find blocks from a cut board, we would act like they were cars. Or a wagon from ’long time ago that had the metal wheel on the outside. And an old tobacco can—you would put on there and bend it. Boy, that thing was fast! But if you ever stepped on it, it was going to hit you in the shin. And there was this one weed that we used to call sun, it was about this [gestures] tall. When it bloomed, the blooms were blue. But when it dried, it was almost like it had whiskers, like it had bits, and we used to race those. We didn’t have shoes because we hardly wore shoes back then.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏢᎮ ᏗᏢᏗ ᏗᏥᏒᏙᏱᏙ ᏱᎨᎮ?
segments.translation: Did y’all ever play with tires or push old tires around?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: Yeah, ᏍᏊᏛ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᏢᏗ ᏏᎾ ᎦᏓ ᏳᏮᎬᏢᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎦᏒᏙᏱᏒ.
segments.translation: Yeah, we did that and then we put dirt in them, too. Boy that dust would be going everywhere.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏓᎬᏒᏗᎲᏛᏲ ᏱᎦ.
segments.translation: It was like it was smoking [with dust].

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏗᎦᏓᎭᏛᏲ ᏱᎦ.
segments.translation: We all would be dirty.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᎸᎯᏳ ᎩᎶ ᎯᎾ ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ ᏱᎩᎣᏍᏕ ᎠᏦᏗ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏱᎪᎮᎵ ᏳᏣᏂ ᎨᏭᏛᏴ ᎤᏂᎩᏓ ᏳᎬᎶ ᏥᎨᎲ.
segments.translation: If there was somebody who was smaller, you’d tell them it was good to ride, and they’d go a little way and then fall out.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏓᏓᏁᎳᏁᎨ ᎾᎥ ᏥᏕᏍᏛᏏᏗᏒ?
segments.translation: Were there houses close by, when y’all were growing up?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏙᏳᎭ ᎦᏲᏟ ᏓᏓᏁᎸ.
segments.translation: Just a few buildings.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎦᏲᏟᏭᎡ, Ꮭ ᏍᎩᏂᎦᏲ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᏯᏁᎮ. ᏙᎮᏂ ᎣᏥᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ.
segments.translation: Just a few, but there were no White people around, we were just all Cherokees.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᏁᎯ ᎦᏚᏏ ᏚᎾᏛᏒ ᎠᏂᏲᏁᎦ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎥᎾᏛᏅᏒᏅ Ꮎ Vanderhiden Mountain ᎠᏃᎮᎰ ᎥᎾ ᏙᏧᎾ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏚᏙᏍᏛᏅ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎥᎾᏂᎩᏒᏅ. ᎢᎦᏗᏅ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏓᎵᏆᏢ ᎤᏂᎷᏤ Ꮎ ᏣᏓᎾᏅ Workman ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎢᎦᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏂᏛᏳᎾᏂᎩᏓ.
segments.translation: There were some that grew up on what they call Vanderheiden Mountain, that was how it got its name, I guess [after the White people]. Some of them came to Tahlequah. There was a store called Workman’s [Department Store], and that’s where some of them owned it.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎥᎾᏭᏍᏲ Ꮲ ᏍᏓᏕᏅ ᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ SalemᎢ?
segments.translation: Were y’all born around Salem?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᎥᎾᏩ ᎮᏂ SalemᎢ ᎠᏩᏕᏅ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏗᏍᏚᎲ ᎣᏦᏎᎲ dam ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᎥᎾ ᎾᎠ ᏦᏤᎲ.
segments.translation: Yeah, I was born there around Salem, we call it the dam that is there, that’s where we lived.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: CC Camp ᎮᏂ ᎤᏃᎮᏗ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏠᎨᏏ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎥᎾ ᎤᏂᏍᏚᎲ ᎥᎾ ᎤᏙᏢᏒ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᏓᏬᏍᏗ. ᎭᎳᏛ ᏂᏕᎨᏥᏅᏒᏂᎳ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ ᎥᎾ ᎨᏥᎠᎷᎩᏏᎯᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎥᎾᏛᏗ ᎨᎪᎮᎸ ᏓᏁᎸᏴ
segments.translation: It was called CC Camp [Civilian Conservation Corps camp], and it was a good place to swim. I wonder how many times these boys got their legs switched being steered away from there? Especially when they had been told to do something at home.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏅᏛᎭ CC ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᏁᎲ ᎥᎾ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏅᏓᏬᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏕᎪᏪᎸ ᎮᏂᏴ ᏱᏂᏕᎦᏝ ᎠᎹ.
segments.translation: Right there where CC used to be, it was good to swim because they marked how deep it was in the water.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: German ᎮᏂ ᎠᏁᏴᎦ ᎠᏁᎮ ᎠᎾᏗᎰ ᎥᎾ ᏢᏅᏴ ᏃᏭ ᏙᎯ ᏄᎵᏍᏓᏂ ᎠᏓᏃᏩ ᏚᏂᏲᏏ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᏍᏓ Ꮕ ᏂᎨᎬᎾᏕᎨ ᎥᎾᏕᎯᏰ ᎢᎦᏗ ᎠᎭᏂ Oklahoma ᎢᎦᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎥᎾᏂᎩᏎ German ᏗᏢ Ꮲ ᏳᏓᎵ Ꮟ ᎩᎶ ᏳᎦᎷᎦ Ꮎ CC camp ᎤᎦᏛᏂᏙ ᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ ᎤᏂᏚᏓ ᎠᎦᏴᎳ ᎤᏕᏅ. ᎤᏂᎪᏩᏛᏗᏭ ᎤᎾᏚᎵᎲ.
segments.translation: They say, a long time ago, there were German prisoners there, and then when the war came to an end, they were treated good. Some stayed there—some of them stayed in Oklahoma. Some went back to Germany. They say every now and then someone still goes over there to CC Camp just to look around and see what it was like, to see where their great grandpa had been.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏲᏛᎭ ᎤᏬᏚ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎩᎳ ᎪᎦ ᏱᎩᏓᏓᏁᎸ ᎮᏂ ᎥᎾ ᎤᏂᏥᎸᏍᎩᎾ ᏓᏫᏒᏅ Easter flowers ᏥᏓᏃᏎ.
segments.translation: It was pretty in the spring, early summer. There was a house there that had a lot of flowers there, Easter flowers…

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: Concrete sidewalk ᏫᏂᏚᏍᏛ ᎡᏧᎳ ᏗᎬᎦᏩᎦᏓ ᏫᏚᏛᏅᏂ ᏏᏲ ᏍᎩᏲ ᏂᏕᎦᎵᏍᏗᎰ ᏞᏲ ᏍᎩᏴ ᏥᏈᏍᏓ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ.
segments.translation: There was a concrete sidewalk, and the flowers grew along there. There isn’t much there nowadays.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎥᎾᏭᏍ Ꮲ Ꮎ CC Camp ᏥᎪᏢ Ꮎ community building ᎥᎾᏭᏍ Ꮲ Ꮎ ᏍᎩᎾ?
segments.translation: Is that place just behind where the CC Camp community building is now?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎤᏒᏛᏭ ᏗᏢ, ᏍᏊᏛ ᎦᏙ ᎨᎲᏍᏊ ᎮᏂ ᏌᏭ ᎤᎳᏍᏗ.
segments.translation: Right behind it, it’s standing on one acre.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᏭ ᏥᎩ ᏫᏍᏛᏓᏅᏖᏝ ᏥᏍᏓᏗ CC Camp ᏃᎴ ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏫᏍᏛᏓᎾᏖᏍᎪ ᎡᏘᏴ ᏥᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ ᎪᎱᏍᏗᎨ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎨᏒ ᏫᏍᏛᏓᎾᏖᏍᎪ boy ᎯᏛ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏕᏗ. ᏍᎩᎨ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏍᏗᎷᏤᎰ ᏳᏓᎭ?
segments.translation: What about now, when you think about CC Camp what do y’all think about ’long time ago? Do y’all think of something good? Boy, it was a good way of life. Is that where you two go to, sometimes?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎯᎠ ᏳᎪᏗ ᏳᏅᏔ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᎣᏂ ᎠᏩᏛᏒ
segments.translation: This One would know more ’cause he’s older than me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎠ ᏕᏣᏓᎳ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎢᏥᏣᎳᎩᎭ ᏕᏣᎵᏍᏕᎵᎮᏅᎭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ
segments.translation: Everybody that lived nearby, you said all you Cherokees were probably helping one another.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏳᏍᏗᏛᏭ ᎨᎲ ᏕᏛᎵᏍᏕᎵᎲ ᎥᎾ ᎮᏂ ᏂᏛᏳᏛᎴᏅ Ꮎ ᎦᏚᎩ ᏣᎾᏗᎰ ᏢᎮᏂ ᏳᎾᏅᏔ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏙᎨᎲ ᎦᏚᎩ ᏳᏂᏪᏍᏗᏭ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ ᎥᎾᏛ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏗᎾᎵᏍᏕᎵᏍᎦ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: That’s how that got started. They don’t really know what that means, Ga-Du-Gi. To them it’s just a saying, Ga-Du-Gi. The Cherokees helped each other back then.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏛᎭ ᎠᏍᎪᎸᎦ ᎦᏚᎩ ᏙᎲ
segments.translation: It’s fading away, Ga-Du-Gi, to help each other, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᎠᎬᏱᏛ ᏣᎩᏛᎦᏅ ᎦᏚᎩ ᎲᏴᏩᏘ ᏱᎨᎵ ᎨᎲ ᎯᎢ Ꮎ ᎣᏍᏛᏢᏅᏢ ᎤᏔᏂᏓ ᏌᏭ Ꮭ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏭᏏ ᏃᏭ ᎠᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎩ ᎮᏅ Ꮎ ᎫᏬ ᏣᎾᏗᎰ ᏥᏭᎨᏛᎵ ᎥᎾ Ꮲ ᏛᏁᎲ Ꮎ ᎦᏚᎩ Ꮫ ᏛᏍᏆᎸᎯ ᎤᏁᏅᏒ ᎢᎦᏛ ᎾᎠ ᏃᏭ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏥᎦᏘᏲᏛ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᎤᏅᏗ. ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᎥᎾᏛᏂ boy ᎣᎦᎵᏍᏓᏅ ᏚᏯ ᏄᏂᎾ ᏒᎯᏰ ᏗᏢ ᏃᎴ ᏙᎩᏍᏆᎵᏒ ᎠᏓ ᎠᏗᎲ. ᎠᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏓᏂᏍᏆᎵᏍᎬ boy ᏒᎯᏰ ᏛᏃ ᏥᎦᏘᏴ ᎤᏩᏈᏴᎡᏗ ᏣᏗᎲᏍᏊ ᎲᎾ ᏄᎾ ᏚᏯ Ꮕ ᏱᎩᎥᏩᏈᏓᏁᎴ
segments.translation: When I first heard the word Ga-Du-Gi [people coming together to help one another], I don’t know if this One was there [Henry]. I’m the only one still alive, but my oldest brother was a preacher. There were some people who were from Mulberry Hollow [Adair County, Oklahoma], and they said they were going to have an event there, around noon. I was waiting for them to say, “It’s time to eat.” We ate beans and taters, and, in the afternoon, we cut wood because they used wood. In the evening I was waiting to get paid, but that was my pay—those beans and taters.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎦᏚᎩ
segments.translation: Ga-Du-Gi!

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: yeah, ᎦᏚᎩ. ᎥᎾ ᏩᏮᏕᎳᏆᎥ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎦᏚᎩ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎩᎳ ᎠᎬᏛᎦᏅ
segments.translation: Ga-Du-Gi! That’s where I learned what Ga-Du-Gi meant. I hadn’t heard it until then.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏛᎭ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎬᏃᎢᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎦᏚᎩ ᏙᎲ
segments.translation: Back then it was alive.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᎩᎶ ᏭᏛᏍᏊ Ꮲ ᏱᏧᏓᏂᎵᏍᏊ. ᎦᏚᎩ ᏯᏁᏂ ᎨᎲ ᎪᎳ ᏱᎩ ᎠᏓ ᏓᏂᏍᏆᎸᏍᎬ ᏃᎴ ᎪᎨ ᏱᎩᎾ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏱᎩ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎠᏂᏟᏏᎲ ᎤᎾᎵᏍᏕᏟᏙᏗ
segments.translation: That’s the way it was. A long time ago when someone was sick, if it was in the wintertime, they would go cut wood for them. And if it was in the summertime, they would go gather wild food for them, to help them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎾᎭ ᎩᎶ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏛᏂ ᏧᏩᏂᏒᏍᏗᎰ ᏧᏁᏅᏒ ᏍᎩᎨ ᏂᏣᏛᏁ ᎨᎮ?
segments.translation: How about when somebody would pass away, they would take the body back to their house to spend the night. Is that what you all did back then?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏍᎨ ᏴᏅᏛᏁ ᎨᎮ ᎪᎮ ᏲᏥᎩᏝ. ᎡᎦᏙᏭ ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: That’s the way they used to do it. But nowadays they don’t. Maybe some still do, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎡᎦᏗᏭ ᏍᎩ ᏱᎾᏅᏛᎩ
segments.translation: Yeah, some still do that.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏭᎪᏛ Ꮎ ᏓᏄᎪ ᏗᏢ ᎠᏁᎯ Ꮟ ᎡᎵ ᏍᎩ ᎾᏅᏛᏁ
segments.translation: I think they mostly still do it out towards Vian [Sequoyah County, Oklahoma].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᏴᏫ ᏧᏩᎾᏓᏟᏏᎰ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏛᏂᏙᎵ
segments.translation: Yeah, people would gather around when that happens.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏲᏛᎭᏲ Ꮟ ᏍᎩ ᏂᏓᏛᏁᎰ. ᏓᏂᏃᎩᏍᎪ ᏃᎴ ᎠᏂᎨᏯ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᎠᏂᏲᎯᎰ ᏒᏃᏯ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᏱᏓᏂᏃᎩ
segments.translation: Yeah, we still do that—they sing, and the women bring food, and they stay till late at night.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᎴ, ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏗᎨᎬ ᏗᏢ ᏍᎩ ᏯᎾᏛᏁ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏙᏱ ᏗᏢ Ᏼ ᏃᎴ ᏳᏃᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏂᏍᎬᏯ ᎥᎾ ᏯᏂᎾ
segments.translation: Yeah, from where I come from, they used to do that, too, and the guys would have a fire built outside.

segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎰ
segments.translation: [together] Yeah, that’s what we do, too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᎮᏃ ᎤᏛᏁᏟᏴᏒᏅ ᎮᏃ yeah
segments.translation: Everything’s changed, yeah.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎡᎵᏛᏲ Ꮟ ᎣᎦᎳᏍᎩ ᎤᏪᏘ ᎥᎾ ᏦᏤᎬ ᏗᏢ ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎡᎵᎦᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏦᏨᏓᏩᏘᎯᏙ ᎩᎶ ᏳᎪᎶᏏ
segments.translation: We still stand in the old ways. We still visit each other when somebody passes away.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏳᎪᎶᏏ yeah
segments.translation: When they pass away, yeah.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎤᏲᏠᏭᎡ ᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᏍᎩ ᏱᏄᎵᏍᏛᎾ ᎩᎳ ᏙᏨᏓᏟᏏᎲ. ᎡᎵᏍᏓ ᎤᎮᏂ Ꮟ ᎣᏍᏓᏭ ᎨᎲ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏏᏓᏁᎸ ᏱᏛᏓᏟᏏ ᎨᎵᎰ. ᎠᏯᎡ ᏏᏓᏁᎸ ᎨᎲᏲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ holiday ᏳᏍᏆᎸ ᎣᏣᏓᏟᏏᎰ ᏕᏪᏅᎲ ᎾᏅᏍᏊ ᏧᏪᏅᎲᏍᏊ ᎠᎾᏓᏟᏏᎰ
segments.translation: I think it’s kind of sad that we don’t visit each other until that happens. I think we should come together as a family before something like that happens. As for me and my family, every time a holiday comes, we get together at my house. They get together at his house, too [Henry].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎦᏍᏗᎲ ᏕᏣᎵᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎪ
segments.translation: So y’all really eat.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᏙᎦᏲᎩᎶᏘᏍᎨ
segments.translation: Till our stomachs swell.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎥᎾᏭ ᎮᏅ ᏱᎩ ᏕᏍᏛᏛᏏᏗᏎ ᏃᎴ ᎥᎾ ᏭᎮ Ꮲ ᎤᏣᏘᏂ Ꮲ ᏫᏣᏕᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏝᎦᏭ ᏱᎩ
segments.translation: So y’all just grew up around there, y’all never lived anywhere else or went anywhere else?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎯᎡᏲ ᎭᏢ ᏗᏢ ᏫᏗᏨᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎴ?
segments.translation: This One, where did you work at? [Henry]

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎾᎥᏭᏅ
segments.translation: Just around here.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎲᏍ ᏄᎾ ᏫᏗᏧᏖᏗ ᏱᎩ Colorado?
segments.translation: Didn’t you dig taters in Colorado?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: yeah, ColoradoᏛ ᏫᎨᏙ ᎨᎲ ᏃᎴ ᎠᏭᏅ ᏙᏦᏛᎸ Ꮎ ᏄᎾ ᏥᏙᏗᎾᏛᏍᎪ ᎥᎾ ᎮᏂ ᏫᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ ᎨᎲ. ᏄᎾ ᏕᎫᏖᏍᎬ
segments.translation: Yeah Colorado, where they grow potatoes. And way up in the mountains, I used to work there picking up potatoes.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏢᎮ broom corn ᏤᏙᎸ ᏱᎩ
segments.translation: Have you ever cut broom corn [sorghum]?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏍᏊᏛ ᎠᏪᏙᎸ ᎥᎾ. ᏧᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗᏭ ᎾᏩᏚᎵᎲᎾ ᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏣᏪᏅᏒ boy ᎢᎳᎦᏯ ᏛᏲ ᏗᎦᎸᏫᏍᏓᏗ Ꮎ broom corn ᎠᎦᎵᏍᏗ
segments.translation: I’ve been there, too [done that]. Just because I didn’t want to go to school—you really had to work to cut that broom corn.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏅ ᏒᎾᏙᏓᏩᏍᏗ ᏧᏩᏪᏙᎸ
segments.translation: I went there for a week.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎩ
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏥᏛᏩᏓᏂᏴ, ᎤᎪᏓ ᎠᏕᎳ ᏓᎩᏫᏛᎲ ᏏᎾ ᏓᎩᏲᏢ ᎨᎲ. ᏂᎯᎾ Ꮲ ᏗᏣᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎵᏙᎸ ᏱᎩ ᏂᎯ?
segments.translation: I ran away from there. I took more money there than I brought back. What about you [Jerry], did you ever work?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏙᏳ ᏛᎨᎲ ᎾᏭ ᏗᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ ᏣᎩᏴᏢ ᏧᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᎠᎩᏅᎪᏨ ᎠᏭ ᏏᏉᏲ ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ ᏣᎩᏴᏟ ᏅᎩ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎢᎠᎩᎷᏥᎾ ᏃᎴ ᏗᎦᏓᏂᏱᏍᎦ ᏥᎾᏩᎵᏍᏛᏅ Stilwell ᏃᎴ ᎥᎾ ᏓᏩᏛᏛᏂ ᏃᎴ ᏓᏩᏕᎶᏆᎥ Ꮎ Connors ᏣᏅᏗᎰ ᎥᎾ ᏓᎦᏍᏋᏗ ᎠᏭ Northeastern ᎠᎩᎷᏨ ᎠᎦᏍᏆᏗᏏᏌᏅ. ᎯᏃ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ ᏨᎩᎾᏢᏅ ᎣᏂᏴ ᏔᎵᏍᎪᎯ ᏦᎢ ᎨᎵ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏗ ᎨᎳᏗᏓ. ᎡᎵᏭᏏ ᏯᎪᎯᎴ ᏱᏛᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎵ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ Ꭿ ᎠᎩᎦᏙᎣᏒ Ꮟ ᎡᏍᎦ ᎾᏮᏁᎲ Ꭿ ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ ᎬᎩᎨᏴᏛᏅ ᎠᏂᏴᏫ ᏄᎾᏛᏅ ᎤᎪᏗ ᎠᏪᏓᏍᏗ
segments.translation: I worked close by, but I joined the military after I graduated Sequoyah for four years. Then I was a cop in Stilwell. When I got rich there, I went to Connors [Connors State College, CSC] and then I came back to Northeastern [State University, NSU] and finished up there. Then I got a job at Cherokee Nation, and I was involved 23 years. I probably would’ve worked there longer but what I experienced in the Army, the Army, kept me from being around a lot of people.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏎᎮ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏣᏕᎶᏆᎡ ᎠᏂᏲᏍᎩ ᎩᎶ ᎯᏃᏎᏗ ᏂᎨᏒᏂ
segments.translation: So, you learned something in the Army that you’re not supposed to tell anybody?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: Ꭰ ᏙᎯᏳᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᏦᎬᎵᎪᎲ Vietnam ᏣᎾᏗᎰ ᎥᎾᎮᏂ ᎪᎯᏓ ᏩᏮᏕᏅ Ꮲ ᎤᏟ ᏱᎩ ᎦᎧᏃᎮᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏯᏩᏕᎳᏆᎡ. ᎤᏲ ᏍᎩᎾᏲ ᎠᎩᏙᎣᏒ
segments.translation: The group that I was with, we were in Vietnam for a long time. But I don’t believe there was anything that was really a secret. I experienced a lot of bad things.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏔᏓᏂᏱᏍᎩ Ꭾ ᏂᏣᎵᏍᏛᏅ
segments.translation: So, you used to be a police officer?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎤᎲ, ᎥᎾᏛ Stilwell ᏑᏓᎵ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏗ ᏃᎴ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏓᎵᏆ ᏓᏩᏕᎳᏆᎢᏟᏅ ᏓᎦᏍᏆᏗ Ꮎ Hastings security guard ᏅᎩ ᎨᎵ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏗ ᏥᏓᏩᏕᎳᏆᎥ
segments.translation: Yeah, at Stilwell for six years. Then, when I came to school at NSU, I was a security guard at Hastings for four years.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏴᏛᏂ ᏲᏁᎩ ᎬᏗ ᎨᎲ hobby ᏯᏅᏗ ᏙᎤᏍᏗ ᏍᏗᎸᏫᎦᏓ ᏍᏛᏛᏗ ᏂᎯ?
segments.translation: Say, for instance in English, they say ‘hobby’, what do you guys like to do?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏗᏙᎯ Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᎩᏂᏃᎲᎵᏓᏍᏗ ᎣᎩᎾᏑᏗᏅ. ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏩᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᏩᎩᎸᏉᏛ.
segments.translation: When we were healthier, we used to like to hunt and fish. But now I just like to eat.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎯᎨ ᎠᏣᏗ ᏗᎦᏂᏱᏍᎩ
segments.translation: So, he was the fisherman?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: yeah, ᎾᏛ ᏗᎦᏘᏍᏗ ᏥᏕᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏦᎢ ᏗᎦᏙᎢᏓ ᏙᎲ?
segments.translation: Yeah, back then we used gigging spears, three-pronged, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏢᎮ ᏗᏍᏗᏪᏄᎩᏍᎦ ᏱᎩ ᏗᎧᏃᎩᏍᏓ
segments.translation: Do y’all scratch [a guitar]?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎲᏛ
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏝᏲ
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎫᎨ ᏱᎬᎩᎸᏥᏲ ᏍᎦᏍᏗ
segments.translation: If I get ticks on me, I do.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᏗᎧᏃᎩᏍᏓ ᏱᎨᎮ? ᎡᎵᏭᎨ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᏱᏕᏍᏗᏃᎩ?
segments.translation: But it’s not a guitar, is it? Could you two sing us a Cherokee song?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏯᏂᏅᎪᏦᏂ ᏛᎮ ᏱᏓᎩᏃᎩᏌ. ᎢᎦ ᏛᏲ ᎠᏩᎨᏩᏒᏗ ᏩᏩᏟᎶᏢ Ꮎ ᏅᏬᏗ ᎬᏗᎲ. ᏂᎮ ᏥᎩᏱᏣᏃᎩᏌ ᏱᏣᎴᏅ ᏳᏫᏥᏍᏆᏓ ᎦᏳᎳ ᏴᏮᎨᏩᏌ ᏂᏣᏪᏒ. ᏙᏛ ᏍᏊᏲ ᏲᏍᎩᏂ ᎪᏪᎵ ᏱᏥᎪᎵᏰ Ꮎ ᏕᏣᎳᏏᏛ ᎢᏍᎩᏃᏎᎸ ᏍᎬᏲ ᎣᏏᏲ ᏱᏓᏩᏙᎵᏥᏏ
segments.translation: They would probably all go out if I sang. It’s gotten to where I really do forget since I use medicine now. Like for instance, if you start a song and you finish, I would already have forgotten what you sung. But if you read us the Bible on what you stand on, I will remember that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎥᎲ yeah, ᎯᎳ ᏂᏥ ᎢᏣᏢᏅᏢ ᏂᎯ
segments.translation: Yeah. How many siblings do you have?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ, ᎯᏍᎩᏛ ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏣ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏮᏏᏅ ᏥᏧᏣ ᏑᏓᎵᏛ ᏃᏥᎥ
segments.translation: There were five girls, and I was the only boy, there were six of us.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏂᎨᏳᏥᎮ ᎨᏣᏒᏙᏱᏙᎮ
segments.translation: The girls used to push you around?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: yeah, ᎬᎦᏍᎫᏛᏂᏏᎶᏍᎬ
segments.translation: Yeah, they used to knock my head around.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏂᎯᎾ ᎭᎳᎩ ᏂᏤᎡ ᎢᏣᏢᏅᏢ?
segments.translation: And you, how many siblings do you have?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏐᏁᎵᏛ ᏃᏥᎥ ᎠᏮᏌ ᎠᏩᏕᎯᏲᏩᏕᎦ, ᏌᏭᎡ ᎠᏩᏓᏚᏥᏴᏍ ᏱᎩ ᏑᏌᏂ? (Asking Henry) ᎠᏩᏓᏚᏥᏴ ᎠᏓᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏴᏅᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎣᎩᏥ. ᎤᏥ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ ᎨᏯᏔᎯ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᎣᏣᏛᎯᏍᏛᎾ ᎠᏩᏛᏐᏂᏛ Mom ᎪᎮᎲ Mom ᎣᎦᏕᎦ ᎢᎪᎯᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮩ ᎤᏥᎢ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᏥ ᏱᏲᎮᎵ ᎡᏍᎦ ᏯᏰᎸᏂ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: There were nine of us, I’m the only one left now, my niece, would it be my niece—Susan? [asking Henry] So, my mom adopted Susan ’cause her mom was wild back in the day. We raised her and she grew up calling my mom, Mom. And if you told her that her biological mom was her mom, she would get upset.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏕᏣᏓᏘᎾᎨ ᏂᎯ?
segments.translation: Do you have kids?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏌᏭ, ᏔᎵᏛ ᎠᎨᏳᏣ ᎠᏧᏣᏅ
segments.translation: One, I mean two—a boy and a girl.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏚᎾᏛᏏᏛ ᎢᏛᎮ ᎦᏳᎳ?
segments.translation: They’re already grown?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎦᏳᎳᏛ ᏧᎾᏛᏂᏲ. ᏨᎩᎵᏌ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᏔᎵ ᎠᏁᎯ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ
segments.translation: Yeah, they’ve grown up. There’s two grandkids now, two boys.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎨ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᎩ?
segments.translation: They talk Cherokee?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎲᎥ, ᏕᎨᏲᎲᏍᎪᎡ ᎦᏁᎳᏗᏍᎪ ᏱᎾᏂᏪᏲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏌᏭ ᎮᏂ ᎯᏍᎩ ᎩᎳ ᏂᏓᏳᏕᏘᏴ ᏐᎢᎾ ᏦᎢ ᎨᎵ
segments.translation: No, I tried to teach them though. One’s fixing to turn five, and I think the other one is three.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: yeah, ᏂᎯᎾ ᎭᎳᎩ ᎾᏂ ᏕᏣᏓᏘᎾ
segments.translation: What about you, how many kids do you have?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᏧᏣ ᎠᎨᏳᏥ ᎨᎲ. ᎠᏧᏣ ᎢᎩᏲᎱᏎᎸ September ᏅᎩᏁ ᎠᏭ ᎠᎾᎳᏍᎬᎵᎲ ᏚᎦᏙᏍᏛ. ᎤᏦᏎᏗ ᎠᏓᏅᏓᏗᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎭᎸᏍᏄᏒ September 4th ᏥᏅᎦᎵᏍᏓ. ᎠᏯᏙᎯ ᎨᎲ SalemᎢ
segments.translation: I have a boy and a girl. But that boy I lost last September while they were playing ball at Sequoyah. I was a little troubled when it turned September 4th. He was a deacon at Salem.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏍ? ᏙᎩ ᏚᏙᎥ ᏍᎩᎾ?
segments.translation: Really? What did you say his name was?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: LeviᏛ ᎠᏃᎮᎲ Ꭰ StephanᎡ ᏚᏙ ᎭᎴ ᎾᏮᎨᏩᏍᎪ ᎠᏮᏏ ᏓᏩᏓᏘᎾᎥ Stephan Cochran ᎠᏎZ ᎵᏫ or Levi ᎠᏃᎮ ᎨᎲ ᏴᏫ. ᏙᎯᏳᏲ ᎣᏣᏠᎪ ᎥᎾ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎮᏂ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏳᏩᏁᎸᏅ ᎨᎰ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎣᎦᏛᏅᏗ. ᎢᎸᏢ ᎢᎾ Crusade ᏥᏛᏍᏆᎸᎯ ᏂᎦᏓᏛ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎾᎦᎵᏍᎦ ᏕᎦᏅᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ speakers. Tent ᎢᎾ ᎤᏔᏂ ᏲᎩᎵᏦᏛᏂ ᏕᎨᏲᎲᏍᎬ ᏳᎾᏛᏅᏗ. ᏃᎴᏅ Falls Creek ᏣᏁᎪ ᏍᎩᏛ ᎠᏛᏅᏍᏗᎰ ᎠᏕᎳ ᎦᏟᏏᎲ ᏓᏘᏁᎪ ᎨᎲ. ᎠᏎᏃ ᏙᏳ, ᏌᏭ ᎠᏫᏄᏥ ᎠᏁᏟᏗ ᏍᏗ ᎤᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ Ꮎ Timo ᏣᏃᎮᎰ Ꮎ ᎤᏔᏂ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎠᎬᏯ ᏗᏢ ᏥᏛᎦᏃᎵᏥᏙᎲ. ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎾᏍᏊ ᏯᏩᏅᏘ Ꮩ ᏚᏙᎥ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Levi—his [first given] name was Stephan. I almost forgot what my own kids’ names were, but we called him Levi. We really miss him around there because he would prepare things when we were going to have an event. We’re going to have this crusade, and he used to lay all the wire out for the speakers, and he would teach them how to put up the tent. When they went to Falls Creek [Youth Camp], he would help gather money for them. But there’s one young man that’s really trying. He’s a big boy who they call Timo. He’s been stepping up front. I don’t really know what his name is.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: yeah, ᎥᎲ ᏥᎪ ᎥᏛᎨᎮ ᏤᏥ ᏙᎲ ᏤᏥ ᎠᏧᏣ?
segments.translation: I’ve probably seen your boy huh?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: yeah, ᏤᏙᎸᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏗᏴᎳᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ, ᎤᏔᏂ ᎠᏧᏣ
segments.translation: Yeah, you’ve seen him—he was light skinned. He was a big boy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏗᏣᎦᏴᎵᎨ Ꮩ ᏧᎾᏙᎢᏓ ᎨᎮ ᏣᏁᎲ
segments.translation: What were your parents’ names [Henry]?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: Jim SawneyᏛ ᏚᏙᎥ ᎡᏙᏓ Rachel ᎢᎾ ᎠᎩᏥ
segments.translation: Jim Sawney was my dad. Rachel was my mom.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: SpringwaterᎢᏍ ᎨᎮ
segments.translation: She was a Springwater, ain’t it? [Rachel’s maiden name]

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: Springwater ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: She was a Springwater.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᏘᏴ ᏤᎲ ᎠᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎩ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏱᎦᏗ ᎡᎵᎦ Sawney ᎪᎱᏍᏗᎨ ᏗᏍᏛᏓᏛᏂ?
segments.translation: Long time ago there was preacher who was short. Alec Sawney. Were y’all related?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎥᎲ yeah
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᎳᏓ ᏥᏂᎦᏛ
segments.translation: He was short.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎤᏍᏗᎡ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏍᎦᏯ
segments.translation: Yeah, he was a little man.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏂᎯᎾᎲ ᏗᏣᎬᏴᎵᎨ
segments.translation: What about you, your parents?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎡᏙᏓᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ Charlie Cochran ᏚᏙᎥ. ᎮᏍᏗ Ꮩ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᎥᎾ ᏂᏛᏳᏛᎴᏅ ᎨᎲ. ᎠᎩᏥᏅᏲ Maggie Sam ᏚᏙᎥ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏰᏟᏴ ᎠᎾᏢᏅᏢ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᏙᏓ ᏃᎴ Ꮕ Floyd Sam ᎪᎯᏓ ᎠᏯᏙᎯ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᎥᎾ SalemᎢ.
segments.translation: My father’s name was Charlie Cochran. I really don’t know where he came from. My mom was Maggie Sam. She was a half-sister to him [Henry]. Floyd Sam was a deacon for a long time at Salem.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: SalemᎢ. ᎾᎮᏂ ᏗᎨᎬ ᏗᏢ ᎠᏁᎯ ᎠᏂCochran ᏧᎾᏙᎢᏓ
segments.translation: Salem. Where I’m from, too, there’s quite a few Cochrans.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: Ꭵ ᏍᏈᏍᏕ, ᎥᎾᏛ ᎠᎴ ᏥᏂᏙᏗᏴᎩᏲᏢ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏗ. Jerry Cochran ᏧᎾᏙᎢᏓ. ᏦᎢ ᏅᎩ ᎴᏱᎩ ᏃᏥᎡ. ᏕᎦᏕᎳᏆᏍᎬ ᏗᎦᏓᏂᏱᏍᎦ ᏴᏩᎵᏍᏙᏗ Miami. Jay ᎦᏚᎲ ᏌᎾᎴ ᏫᏙᏍᏛᏟᏒ ᎠᏭ ᏓᎷᏫ ᎡᎯ ᏌᏭ ᎠᏧᏣ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᏍᏊ ᏄᏰᏟᏛ ᏍᎩᏴ ᏬᎩᏂᎷᏨ. ᏌᎾᎴᏭ ᏣᏁᎵᏭ ᏬᏨᎴᏂᎲᏛ ᏌᏭ truck ᏙᎯ ᎠᏓᏟᏒ ᎠᎩᎦᏖᏃᎸ ᏫᏥᏯᏕᏲᎸ. ᏫᏥᏯᏕᏲᎵᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎥᎾ ᏗᏓᏂᏱᏍᎩ ᎤᎲ ᏫᏛᎩᏧᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᎤᏟᏗᏢ ᏩᏩᎴᏫᏍᏛᎾ driver's license ᎤᎦᏔᏲᏎᎵ ᏫᏥᏅᏁᎵ ᎤᎪ Jerry Cochran. Boy ᎤᏏᏅᏒ ᎦᎶᏪ ᎤᏭᏍᎩᏒ wait a minute ᏥᏲᎮᎸ. ᎾᎯᏳ ᏄᏒ Ꮎ Ꮩ ᏚᏙ Ꮎ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎥᎾ Bull Hollow ᎡᏍᏗᏢ ᎠᏩᏅᏔ Old GreenᎢ ᏱᎩ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ?
segments.translation: Yeah, there’s a lot of them. One time I about got shot up that way. There was a Jerry Cochran. There’s about three or four of us [different Jerry Cochrans] when I was going to school to be a cop at Miami. Me and a friend of mine were going through Jay one early morning, I don’t know why we were going that way. We started at eight in the morning and there was a truck going slow, I went around him. There was a cop sitting there. He flipped his lights on, and I stopped, and he asked for my driver’s license. He seen ‘Jerry Cochran’ and he pulled his pistol out and backed up. I said, “Wait a minute.” What’s the name of that church on this side of Bull Holler [Bull Hollow]?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Oh yeah, ᎤᏪᏘ ᎢᏤᏍᏛᎢ
segments.translation: Oh yeah, Old Green?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎥᎾ ᎾᎠ ᎤᏛᏒ ᎡᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ jerry Cochran ᏗᎦᏚᎴᏂ ᎤᏓᏃᏍᎩᏓ ᎨᎮ ᎤᏒᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ. Boy ᎠᎭᏂᏛ ᏃᏭ ᏥᏩᏘ ᎤᏪᎵᏎ ᎮᏂ. ᎠᏫᏄᏥᏭᏅ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ ᎦᎶᏪ ᎦᏁᎲ ᎦᏂᎵᏛ ᎤᏛᏓᏍᏛᏁ ᏏᏅ radio ᏥᏕᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎢᏅᎯ ᎨᎲ Jay, Stilwell ᎢᎾ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏧᎾᏓᏛᎦᏁᏗ. ᎦᏂᎵᏛ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏚᎾᏝᏃᎮᏢ ᎲᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏲᎩᏂᏟ ᎣᎩᏃᎯᏙᏗ ᏦᏍᏛᏓᏂᏱᏍᎦ ᎨᎲ. ᏙᏛᏲ Ꮭ ᏱᎬᏩᎨᏩ. ᏃᎴ Ꮠ ᏦᏤᎬ ᎾᎥ ᎡᎯ ᎠᏫᏄᏥ trailer house ᎤᏔᎾ ᎤᏩᏎ ᏫᏚᏲᏎᎾ boy ᏅᎾ ᎠᏯ ᎤᏠᏯ ᏚᏙᎥ ᎠᏯ ᎣᎩᎾᏂᎾᏟᎲ ᎠᏭᏛ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏦᎩᏂᏍᏚᏗ ᎯᎢ ᎦᏂᎵ ᏑᏕᏘᏳᏓ Ꮲ ᎤᏟᎩᎵᏙᎸ ᎣᏍᏗ ᏣᏃᎯᏍᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᏙᏛ ᎠᎩᏴᏘᏟᏙᎸ ᏓᏩᏙᎥ
segments.translation: Yeah. There was an old man there who stole a car there, that previous night. He probably thought, “I found him right here.” Because that cop was a young man. His gun was shaking. He was really trying to listen to his radio. It was far—from Jay to Stilwell. He could barely talk. And we didn’t have anything to prove who we were—going to be cops. You really couldn’t forget that [incident]. And, there was another young man who lived down our way who bought a big trailer house. We had the same name, and he wasn’t paying for it [the trailer house]. And they tried to make me pay for it. And they were about to take us to jail. It took about a year to straighten that out. I’ve had some bad luck having that name.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᏍᏊ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏗ ᏄᎬᏫᏳᏒ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᏗᏓᏂᏱᏍᎩ ᏩᎩᏩᏛᎯᏙᎸ. Ꮲ ᎸᎯᏳ ᏣᏓᏅᏖᏢ ᏱᎩ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᏗᏓᏂᏱᏍᎩ ᏂᏣᏣᏍᏙᏗ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ. ᎲᎥ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏙᏅ ᏯᏩᏚᎵᏛ ᎦᏣᏓᎯᏕᏗ ᏱᎩᏱᏍᎩᏍᏕᎳ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ, ᏗᎠᎮ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ. ᏔᎵ ᏳᎾᏙᏛᏩᏍᏗ ᏭᏅ ᏗᏣᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ ᏱᎦᏬᏎᎸ. ᎾᎯᏳ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏔᎵ ᏳᎾᏙᏛᏩᏍᏗ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎠᏯᏲ ᏣᏇᏯ, ᎲᎥ ᎡᎵᏭᏛ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏚᎸᎮ. ᎣᎩᎾᎵ ᎠᏲᏁᎦ ᎠᏧᏣ ᏗᏓᏂᏱᏍᎩ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏢᏴ ᎤᎷᏨ ᏓᏁᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᎩᎾᎵ ᏗᎲᏣᎦ ᎠᏬᏎᎸ ᏗᎾᏓᏂᏱᏍᎩ ᎤᏦᏙᏗ ᎤᏦᏛᏃ ᎣᎩᎾᏣᏅ ᎣᏍᏗᎦᏖᏃᎵᏙᎲᏅ ᏃᎴ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᏫᎦᏅᎪᏨᏃᏅᏭ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏙᏩᎴᎵ ᏬᏍᏛᎴᏫᏍᏙᏛᏅ ᎠᏨᏍᏗ ᏭᎸᎲ ᏄᏩᏁᎸ. ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎢᎦᎵᏍᏓᏂᏙᎸ ᏩᏢᏃᎮᏢᎢ ᎠᏬᏎᎸ. ᎠᎦᏍᎦᏯᏗᏛ ᎠᏩᏣᎣ. ᏄᏩᏃ ᎠᏨᏯᏍᏗ ᏩᏱᏐ ᎦᎵ ᎨᎵᏍᎪᏛ ᎦᎶᏪᏃ ᏗᎦᏂᏙᎮᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎨᎵᏍᎪᏛ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎣᏍᏗᏭ ᏄᎵᏍᏓᏂᏙᎸ. ᏃᎴ ᏧᎾᏗᏔᏍᏗ ᏙᎩᎾᎴᏫᏍᏛᏅ ᏫᏂᎦᏖᏃᎵᏓ ᎤᏛᏅ Ꮓ ᎣᏍᏗᎦᏖᏃᎵᏙᎲ ᏦᎦᎵᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏂᏯᎥ ᏧᎾᏗᏔᏍᏗ. ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏕᎬᏮᎧᏂᏍᎪ. ᏄᎳ ᎢᏂᏅᎪᎢ ᏥᏲᏎᎰᏛ ᏏᏛ ᎠᎦᏖᏃᎰ ᏛᎦᏙᏍᏗᎰ ᎠᏂᏴᏫ ᎾᏅ ᏦᎩᏂᏅᎪᏥ Ꮓ ᏔᎵᎭ ᏫᏄᏒᏢ ᏃᎾ ᏄᎬᏫᏳᏒ ᏗᏓᏂᏱᏍᎦ ᎭᏓᎯᏕᏧ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ, ᎲᎥ ᏥᏲᏎᎸ, ᏥᏈᏍᏓᏅ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏗᏮᎾ ᎠᏂᏯᎥ ᏧᎾᏗᏔᏍᏗ ᎬᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏍᎩᏅ ᏱᎬᎩᎸᏂ ᏱᏗᎦᏥᏍᏚᏂ. ᎦᎾᏰᎦ ᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ
segments.translation: One time, the chief of police came to my house and asked me if I ever wanted to be a cop. I told him no and he said, “If you have time, I’d really like for you to help us out. You just have to go to school for two weeks,” at that time it was just two weeks. They said they would pay for it but I told them that’s OK. A young friend of mine became a cop. He came over to the house and he asked me to get in the police car with him. I got in, we looked around and, just outside of town, we pulled a car over. He pulled out his flashlight and said, “If something happens, let somebody know on the radio.” I was scared, sitting in there. He was waving his flashlight as he walked towards the car. And I thought, “Gah-lee, what if that guy had a gun?” But everything worked out. And then we stopped at a bar, and we looked around. Some of my friends were in there, they were really looking at me. “Let’s hurry up and get out,” I said. But he was still looking around at people. Two days later the chief of police called me again and asked me again if I was interested. I said no—there was a lot of my relatives in that bar, they’d probably beat me up if I took them to jail. It was dangerous, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: yeah, ᎨᎲᏛ ᎪᎯᎩ ᏥᎩᏢ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎬᎵᏍᏙᏗ ᏗᎦᏓᏂᏱᏍᎦ ᏱᏂᎦᎬᎵᏍᏓ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᏒ ᎠᏚᎩᏍᏓ ᎾᏭᎮᏂ ᎾᏅ marijuana ᏣᏃᎮᎰ ᏍᏊᏛ ᏱᎩᎡᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᎩ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎩᎶ ᎤᏴᏍᏕᏓ ᏱᏍᏓᏠᏏ ᎤᏓᎸᏫᏉᏗ ᏂᎵᏃᎮᏗᎲᎾ ᏱᎩ ᎡᎵᏭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏱᏣᏛᏓᏍᏓᏏ ᎨᎲ. ᏱᏣᏏᏁᏂᏭ ᎮᏂ ᏗᎦᏚᎴᏂ ᏗᏣᎲ ᏗᏢ ᏱᏣᏍᏓᏩᏚᎦ ᎮᏂ ᏦᎮᎲ ᎾᎠᏅ ᏳᏫᏯᏘᏃᏟ ᏳᏫᏯᎠᎩ ᎨᎲ. Boy ᎪᎯ ᏍᎩᏂ ᏥᎩ ᏲᎮ ᎦᎶᏪᏛ ᏚᏂᎳ ᏂᎦᏗᏭ. ᎾᎾ ᏍᏊᏅ ᏣᎾᏟᏴᏎᎯᏍᏗ ᎤᏁᎦ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎠᎾᏗ ᎮᏍᏓ ᎮᏂ ᏳᎾᏙ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎲ ᏍᏊ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᏧᎾᏝᏂᎩᏓ ᎾᏅᎵᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: Yeah, it would have been. But nowadays, there ain’t no way I’d want to be a cop ’cause, back then, all there was was alcohol and marijuana. That’s all there was. Back then, if somebody was just drunk, and you didn’t talk roughly to them, they would listen to you and follow you back to your car. He would argue with you for a little bit, but then he would just go with you. But, nowadays they’ve got guns and that white stuff that they sniff. They don’t know what they’re doing, and it also makes them strong.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᎮᏂ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏗᏔᏍᏗ ᏭᏅ ᏱᎩ ᏥᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ
segments.translation: But at that time, it was just alcohol at work.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎥᎥ, ᎠᏗᏔᏍᏗ ᎤᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏦᎳ
segments.translation: Yeah, just alcohol and tobacco.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎥᎥ, ᎾᎾ Ꮲ ᏍᏊ ᏳᏍᏓ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎦ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᎮᏎᏂ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏱᎩᏥᎦᎾᏰᎬ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎦ ᏥᎩ. ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏰᏟ ᏔᎵᏁ ᎣᏣᏢᏅᏢ ᏗᎾᏗᏔᏍᎩ ᎨᎲ ᏍᏊᏅ ᏱᏙᎦᏥᏍᏚᎲᏍᎩ ᎨᎵᏍᎬ
segments.translation: They didn’t use stuff like that back then. But it was still dangerous. My half-brothers and cousins were always drinking, and I would probably be having to put them in jail, I was thinking.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ ᏍᏛᎴᏅ ᎭᏢ ᏍᏛᎴᏅᎮ ᎥᎾᏍ Ꮲ ᎪᏢᏍᎡ SalemᎢ
segments.translation: What about when y’all first started school, was there a school close to Salem?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: yeah, ᎥᎾᏛ ᎠᏩᎴᏅᎲ ᏝᎦ. ᏦᎬᏓᏅᏒᏅ ᏦᏤᎲ ᏭᎨᏓᎵᏴ Fog Holler ᏚᏙᎥ ᎥᎾ ᎠᎩᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏭᏁᏍᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ Ꮓ ᏬᎩᎶᏒ ᎦᎵᏉᎦ ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏬᎩᎶᏏ ᎣᎦᏓᏅᏏ ᎥᎾ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ. ᎥᎾᏅ ᏩᏮᏛᏐᏅᏃ
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s where we started. But we moved from where we were living to down the holler—it was called Fog Holler. Dad built a house there; I was seven years old when we went there. When we moved from the creek, that’s where I grew up.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎥᎾ ᏛᎭ ᏕᏣᏕᎵᏆᎥᏅ Star of Bethlehem ᏣᎾᏗᎰ ᎥᎾ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ
segments.translation: Where that Star of Bethlehem church is, that was a school and that’s where you started.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎪᏢ ᏃᏭ ᏙᎲ
segments.translation: There’s a church there now, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏙᏛ Ꭽ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᏳᎾᏛᎾᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏔᎵᎭ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎾᏓᏟᏏᎰ ᏑᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᎨᎲ. ᏃᏭᏂ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲᏲ ᎥᎾ ᎮᏂ BellᎢ ᏥᎩ ᎥᎾ ᎮᏂ ᏫᏓᎩᏁᏗ degree
segments.translation: I don’t know what they do now—they gather about twice a year. As for me, I got my degree at Bell [Bell Community School, Adair County, Oklahoma].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎥᎾᎮ ᏣᏌᎹᏗ ᏫᎾᏣᎵᏍᏓᏁ. ᏗᏍᏗᎬᏴᎵᎨ ᏧᏂᎬᏴᎵᎨ Ꮩ ᏧᎾᏙᎢᏓ ᎨᎮ?
segments.translation: That’s where you got smart. What were the names of your parents’ parents? [grandparents]

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᎨᎲ Bill Springwater ᏚᏙᎥ ᎠᎩᏚᏓ ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩᏅ Jenny Sevenstar ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Bill Springwater was my grandpa, and Jenny Sevenstar was his wife.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Jenny Sevenstar, ᏂᎯᎾ?
segments.translation: Jenny Sevenstar. And you [Jerry]?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛᏲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᎡᎵᏭ ᎯᎢ ᏳᏅᏔ
segments.translation: I don’t know. This One [Henry] might know.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏗᎦᏅᎪᏫᏍᎩᏍ?
segments.translation: Diganvgowisgis? [referring to a name]

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎲᏍ ᏗᎾᏓᏅᏟ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: Was that Dad’s brother?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏍᏊᏛ ᎭᏙ ᏗᎾᏓᏅᏟ, ᎮᏍᏗ ᏛᏲ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᏃᏭ ᏣᏙᏗ
segments.translation: Yeah, I think that was his brother. I didn’t know about your dad.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏥᎦᏗ ᏕᎦᏝᏙ ᎮᏂ ᏗᏢ ᎤᏛᏒ ᎧᏃᎮᏍᎪ ᎮᎲ. ᎠᎯᏂᏅ ᏗᏢ ᎤᎷᏣᏅ ᎠᏂStarr ᏥᎩ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎬᏮᎾᏢᏁ ᏃᏩ ᎬᏲᎱᏍᎦ. ᎡᏥᎾ ᏥᎨᎲᏃ ᏙᏳ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᏚᎾᏙᎥ ᎥᎩᎵᏌ. ᎥᎾᎡ Ꮎ Sally Bull ᏣᎾᏗᎰ ᏭᎵᏍᏛ ᏭᎨᏛᎵᏴ Ꮲ ᎤᏛᏒ ᎨᎮᏲ
segments.translation: That’s what I’m saying. He grew up around Braggs [Muskogee County, Oklahoma], is what he used to say. When he came down this way, the Starr’s hired him, until he passed. And Mom, I really don’t know the names of my grandparents. She grew up way up the holler they call Sally Bull [Sally Bull Hollow].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᏗᏍᏗᎦᏴᎵᎨ Ꮭ ᎠᎸᎯᏳ ᎤᏂᏃᎮᏢ ᏱᎨᎲ ᏚᎾᏓᏩᏛᎲ
segments.translation: Did your parents ever tell you where they met?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎲᎥ Ꮭ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: No, not me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎤᎾᏕᏞᎨ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏳᏰᏟᏗ ᏳᎾᏅᏔ ᎠᏁᎵᎮ
segments.translation: I guess they kept it a secret, I guess they thought y’all didn’t need to know.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎾ ᏗᏍᏗᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᎾᏛᏁ ᎨᎮ ᎢᏣᎵᏍᏕᎵᏙᏗ ᏢᏍ ᏚᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎮ ᎭᎴᎨ
segments.translation: How about your parents [Henry], what did they do to provide for y’all. Did they work somewhere?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏓ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎠᏓᏭ ᏧᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ ᎨᎮ. ᎠᎩᏥᎾ ᎨᎲ ᎡᎵᏏ ᎢᎾ ᎨᎲ Ꮓ ᎪᎱᏍᏗᏭ ᎠᏛᏔᏅᏍᎩ ᎥᎾ ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎰ ᎨᎲ ᏚᏯ ᏱᎩ ᎠᏂ
segments.translation: My dad worked in the woods. Cutting wood, and things like that. My mom worked in a garden, with fruits and vegetables like beans and strawberries.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏂ yeah
segments.translation: Strawberries, yeah.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲᏅ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᏂStarr ᎬᏩᎾᏝᎥ ᏩᎦ ᏧᎦᏎᏍᏓ ᎨᎲ ᏙᏱ ᎠᏁᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ. ᎧᏃᎮᏍᎪ ᎡᏲ ᎨᎲ Ꮟ ᏕᎦᏝᏓ ᏥᏛᏰᎲ ᏐᏈᎵ ᏙᏗᏂᎯᎴᎬ ᏩᎦ ᏗᏐᏯ ᏳᏓᏅᎯᏓ. ᏔᎵᎭ ᏥᎢᎭ ᏧᏒᎯᏓ ᏬᏥᎶᏍᎬ ᎠᏗᎲ. ᎯᎠᏃ ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎴ ᎥᎾ ᎬᏲᎱᏒ ᏩᎦ ᏚᎦᏎᏍᏛ. ᏓᏗᎲᏂ ᏩᎦ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏧᏁᎩᎡᏓ ᎡᎵᏭ ᎣᎦᎵᏍᏕᏝᏙᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᎣᎩᏥᏅ ᏣᏗᏃ ᎯᎢ ᎠᏛᏔᏅᏍᎬ ᎤᏭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎥᎾᎦᏎᏍᏓ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᎪᎦᏎᏍᏓ. ᎤᎪᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎡᎾᎥ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎬᎩᏍᏓ. ᎪᎯᎾ ᏥᎩ ᏱᏓᎾᎵᏍᏋᏴᏍᏗᏛ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏱᏓᏝᏁᎵ
segments.translation: As for my dad, he worked with the Starr’s, with cattle. They were always outside. And he did mention one time that he lived at Braggs. And they drove cattle from there to Fort Smith [Sebastian County, Arkansas]. Sometimes it would take two or three days. And he worked there until he passed away, watching cattle. He would pen some up to get milk. And, then Mom would work picking fruit. And then just work around the house taking care of the kids. There was a lot of stuff, back then, we could eat. Nowadays children would make a sour face at what you put on the table.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎡᏆᏩᎨ ᏕᏥᏫᏒᏁ ᎾᎯᏳ?
segments.translation: Did y’all have a big garden back then?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏲᏛᎭ ᎠᏂᏫᏒᏍᎩ ᎨᎲᏲ
segments.translation: Oh yeah, they used to have big gardens back then.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏎᎷᏛᎭ, ᏚᏯ
segments.translation: Corn and beans.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏓ ᎠᎮ ᏣᏛᏍᎪ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏓ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏛᏲ ᏱᎩᏓ ᎠᏂᏫᏒᏍᎬᏲ ᎾᎯᏳ
segments.translation: A lot of different things. It really grew back then, and they grew a lot.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᏗᏥᎨᏃ mason jar ᏥᏕᎲ ᎡᏘᏴ
segments.translation: Did your moms have Mason jars, a long time ago?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎦᎶᏔᏅᏍᎩ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: She was a canner.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏙᏓᏲ ᎠᎵᏍᏕᎵᏙᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᎶᏔᏅᏍᎪ
segments.translation: That really helped us out, her canning.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎦᎶᏔᏅᏍᎬ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏕᎬᏗᏍᎨ
segments.translation: When they were canning, that’s what they used [Mason preserving jars].

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏆᏂ ᏛᎭ ᎾᏅ ᏚᏯ ᏧᏓᎴᏅᏓ ᏓᎹᏟ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎠᏩᏝᎪ ᏄᏰᏟᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎦᏂᏝ ᎭᏫᎾ ᏗᏢ ᏥᏓᏂᎲᏍᎬ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᏂᏴ ᏩᏮᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᎾᏅ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᏳᏴᏝ ᏂᏕᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ Ꮎ ᏚᏢᏅᏙ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᏳᏃᎸᎾ ᎥᏥ ᏱᏗᏴᎯ. ᏄᎦᏃᏮ ᎢᏅ ᎤᏂᏰᎸᎲ ᎥᎾ ᎭᏫᎾ ᏓᏂᎲᏍᎨ
segments.translation: Peaches and beans and other things—tomatoes. I couldn’t figure out why they put them all under the bed. Then I figured out the house got so cold, ’cause there were cracks in the house, and the snow would blow in. The wind would blow through there. So I guess they were just storing it where it was a little warmer.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏂ ᎾᎯᏳᏃ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎡᏙᏓ ᎠᏥᎵ ᏅᏃ Ꮎ railroad ᎥᎾᏃ ᏧᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ ᎨᎲ Kansas cityᏢ ᏪᏙᎰ ᎨᎰ ᏫᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎰ
segments.translation: As for me, my dad—back then my dad worked on the railroad. And he used to go up to Kansas City.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᏍᎦᏍᏗᎨ ᎨᏣᎾᏝᎡ ᏨᏌᏅ ᎯᏧᏣ ᎨᎮ
segments.translation: So, did they really work you hard, since you were the only boy?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎥᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎠᎹᎨ ᏕᎯᎾᏥᏙᎮ?
segments.translation: Did you carry water?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᎸᎯᏳᏅ
segments.translation: Sometimes.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᏍ ᎠᎹᏟᏗᏍ ᎢᏦᏢᏎ ᏗᏤᏅᏒ ᎾᎠ ᎪᏢᏎ ᏗᏤᏅᏎ ᎥᎾᏢ Ꭸ ᎦᏂᏅᎪᎬ ᏫᏗᏥᏁᎩᏍᎨ?
segments.translation: Was there a well by your house, or was there a spring somewhere you went and got it?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎦᏅᎪᎬᏛ ᎥᎾᏭ ᏫᏙᏥᏁᎩᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ Fog Holler ᏧᏬᎩᎷᏨ ᎥᎾ ᎡᎵᏍᏊ ᎨᏴ ᎨᎲ ᏛᎦᏅᎪᎬ ᎥᎾᏅ ᏫᏙᏥᏁᎩᏍᎪ
segments.translation: There was a spring, when we moved to Fog Holler, and it was quite a ways away, and we would get it [water] there.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏅ ᏢᎮ Ꮎ football ᎥᎾᎳᏍᎬᏟᏗ ᏥᏂᎦᏅ ᏍᎩᏴ ᎨᏛᎵ Ꮟ ᏃᏩᏥᎩ ᎬᏅᎪᎦ ᎥᎾ ᏥᏈᏍᏓ ᏴᏩ ᏧᏂᏁᎩᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏱᏚᎧᏲᏏ ᏙᏩᎴᎵᏛ ᏱᎩᏚᏂᏅᏙ ᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏬᏥᏁᎩᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: It was about the length of a football field—where we used to get it. There were a lot of people there. Sometimes there would be rows of cars.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎨ ᎡᎮᎨ Ꮎ ᎠᏥᎵ ᏣᎾᏗᎰ?
segments.translation: Was there watercress there?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏏᏛ ᎡᎭ ᏃᏭ ᏥᎦ
segments.translation: There still is.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᎯᏭᏍ boy Ꮩ ᎤᏖᏗ ᎠᎩᏍᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Boy, they were good to eat, back then.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᎠᏎᎾ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎦᏗ ᏱᏕᎨᏣᎵᏍᏆᏴᏍᏓᏍᏛ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏱᎦᎯᏝᏁᎵ
segments.translation: If you fed that to the kids nowadays, it’d give them a sour face.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎤᎤᎤ ᏯᎾᏗ ᏛᎭ ᏙᎲ
segments.translation: “Eeeewww!” they would say, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: yeah, ᎪᏧᏂᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏣᏃᎮᎲ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏥᎩᏍᎩ ᎨᎲ ᏜᏱᏕᏅ
segments.translation: And kochani, too, they would say. We ate that, and poke salad.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏓᏬᎵ
segments.translation: Mushrooms.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏒᎩ
segments.translation: Onion.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏒᎩᎾ ᏃᎴ ᎧᏩᏯᏅ
segments.translation: Onions and huckleberries.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: (Unintelligble)

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏓᏬᎵᏃ
segments.translation: And mushrooms.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏓᏬᎵᏛᎾ
segments.translation: Yes, mushrooms.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Boy ᏙᎲ ᎤᏖᏗ ᎢᏓᎵᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎨ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Boy, we really ate good back then, huh?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎾᎯᏳᎡ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎾᏛᏍᏊ Ꮎ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᎯ ᏳᏍᏗᏭ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏥᎩᏍᎬ Ꮎ ᎭᏫᏯ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Oh yeah, back then. And we used to eat everything from the woods. And meat.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: yeah, yeah ᏏᏆᎨ ᏍᏊ ᏗᏥᏁᎦᎵᏍᎩ ᎨᎮ?
segments.translation: Did you all skin pigs back then?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: Yeah
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: Yeah
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎤᏓᏁᎸᏛ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏚᏒᏓᎾᎸ ᏅᏱᎾ ᎤᏰᏍᏓᎥ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏔᎵᎭ ᏱᏚᏂᏝ ᎥᎾ ᎠᏝᎲᏍᎬ ᎭᏫᏯ ᎠᎻᏅᏃ ᎤᎪᏗ ᏄᎾᏅ ᏱᎩᏓᏂᏍᎪᏍᎬ ᎧᏁᏍᎦ ᎠᎭᏍᎬ ᎭᏫᎾ ᎥᎾ ᏓᎲᏍᎬ ᏄᎾ ᏃᎴ ᎥᎫᏢᏍᎬ Ꮓ ᎪᎳ ᏗᏢ ᏱᎩ ᏗᎭᏗ
segments.translation: Yeah. My dad had some shelves and some rocks for a floor. When they killed two [pigs], they would put the meat there and salt them. And, if it was potatoes, they would dig a hole, and they would put hay in it, then potatoes, and cover it back up. Then, in the winter, we would take them out.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏧᎵᎦᏏᎨ ᏍᏗᎸᏉᏗ ᏍᏗᎩᏍᏗ?
segments.translation: Do you two like to eat chitlins [pig intestine]?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏕᎬᏂᏍᎡ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᎩᎸᏉᏕ
segments.translation: No, not while they were cooking.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎡᎦ ᎮᏂ ᏗᎩᎸᏉᏗ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, I liked them.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏳᏅᏏ ᏍᎩᏂᏲ ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏂᎦᏛᏁᎲ
segments.translation: But when they got done, I would really eat them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏛ ᎦᏩᏒᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ
segments.translation: Gaaaw, it really stunk, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᏂᏒᎩᏛᏲ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, they really smelled.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏙᏯᏛᏲ ᏱᏕᏣᏩᏒᎩ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, it really did smell.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎦᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᏱ ᏗᏢ ᏥᎬᏂᏍᏗᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏓ
segments.translation: I remember Grandma used to cook them outside.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ ᎠᏣᏗ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎣᏂ ᏗᏢ ᏭᏩᎧ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏱᏗ ᎥᎾᏛ ᏒᎩ ᎴᏱᎩ Ꮎ wild onions
segments.translation: Nowadays, [for] things like fish and wild onions—they have a stove out back.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏜᏱᏕᏅ
segments.translation: And poke salad.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎤᏯᎲᏗ ᏙᏳ ᎤᏢᏗ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ ᎠᏎᎾᏅ ᎤᏠᎢᏴ Sally Bull ᎥᎾ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ Ꮟ ᎡᎭ ᎠᎾᏗᎲ. ᎬᎩᏲᎮᎰ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎬᏂᏍᏛᏃᏅ ᎦᏳᎳ
segments.translation: That bean vine is hard to find nowadays. But they say you can find them down in Sally Bull, they’re by the water. They used to bring me some that was already cooked.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ? Ꮎ ᎤᏴᎭᏗ
segments.translation: What exactly is that?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: bean vine ᎨᎵ ᎠᏃᎮᎰ
segments.translation: They say it’s a bean vine, I think.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: bean vine, ᎦᎴᎩᏛ
segments.translation: Bean vine, it climbs.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: green briar ᎤᎮᏂ ᏰᎵ ᏂᏣᏛᏂ ᏱᎦ
segments.translation: You would think it was a green briar.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Ꮭ ᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏩᏁᏟᏔᏅ ᏱᎩ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏓ
segments.translation: I’ve never tried anything like that.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: Ꮂ?
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: Ꮭ ᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏩᏁᏟᏔᏅ ᏱᎩ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ
segments.translation: I’ve never tried anything like that.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏢᎩ? ᎤᎦᎹᏛ ᏭᎪᏛ ᎨᎲ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ Ᏼ ᏱᎩᏱᏄᏂᏓ ᏯᏂᎦᎭᎷᏱ ᎨᎲ Ꮓ ᏯᏅᏂᏍᏓ ᎤᎦᎻᏅ Ꮓ ᎤᎪᏗ ᏎᎷ ᎦᏚ ᏱᎩ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏯᏑᏴᎦ
segments.translation: Really? It’s kind of a soup. They would cut this much up [gestures] then they cook it into soup, and eat it with corn bread.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎠᎩᏲᏏᏛᏃ
segments.translation: I’m hungry now.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏫᏨᏩᏛᎯᏙᎸ ᏏᏭ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎯᏲᏢᎢ
segments.translation: Next time I stop by, make some.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏱᎦᏥᏲᏏ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ ᏙᎮᏂ ᏯᏂᏲᎩ ᎮᏂ. ᏥᏍᏛᏂ ᎴᏱᎩ ᏙᎦᏥᏩᏎᎰ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎢᏅᎯ ᎮᏂ ᏗᏁ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏧᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᏗ. ᏌᏭ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏙᏩᎴᎳ ᏱᏤ ᎥᎾ. ᏗᏣᏍᏆᎸᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏱᏚᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏏ ᏳᏛᏯᏅ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏫᏓᏴᏗ ᏃᎴ ᏫᏙᎦᎪᏗ
segments.translation: OK. I’ll tell them boys, and I’ll buy some crawdads from them, too. Because they live too far-away-back-in-there to work. They only have one good car. They’ll really work hard if you go get them, but you must go get them and take them back.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏍ?
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏓᏁᎸ ᎮᏂ ᎦᏥᎾᏝᎣ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏳᏓᎭ
segments.translation: Sometimes I put them to work at the house.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏩᎴᎳ Ꭾ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᏗᏅᏁᎭ?
segments.translation: Do they fix cars?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏱᎾᏓᏅᎩᏛ
segments.translation: They can, yeah.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏍᏊᏛ ᎣᏍᏓ
segments.translation: They can do that good.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎮᏂ ᏓᏒᎸᏓ hood!
segments.translation: They should, the hood is always up!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎨ ᏭᎨᏛᎵᏴ ᏥᏗᏁ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ?
segments.translation: Is that those boys who live in the holler?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎥᎥ, ᎥᎾᏛᏃ ᏭᎵᏍᏓᏭ ᏫᎦᏅᏅ ᎤᎵᏍᏆᏟᏗ ᏗᏓᏁᎳ ᎥᎾ ᏭᎵᏍᏓ
segments.translation: Where the road ends. The last house is where they live.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎩ ᏧᎾᏙᎩᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: What are their names?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᏂ ᏌᏂᏛ ᎠᏂSawney ᏂᎦᏗᏛᏅ ᎠᏂFlynn
segments.translation: The Sawneys, all of them, and the Flynns.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: Sally Bull HollerᎡ ᎠᏃᎮᎰ ᎥᎾ
segments.translation: They call it Sally Bull Hollow .

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎢᏥᎦᏘ ᏱᎨ ᎥᎾ ᏂᏛᏳᏛᎴᏅᏗ
segments.translation: Is your pastor from there?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎥᎾᏛ ᏥᏛᏁᎲ ᎠᏧᏣ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, he lived there when I was a boy.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏓ ᎠᎵᏥᏙᎲᏍᎦ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: He was a good preacher.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: yeah, ᎥᎾ ᏛᏍᏊ ᏂᏓᏳᏛᎴᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ Lawrence ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: That is where Lawrence came from too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏍ? Well, I’ll be...
segments.translation: Really? Well, I’ll be...

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏗᏍᏗᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏥᎨᏒ ᏃᎴ ᏍᏗᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎤᏂᏁᏍᏛᏅ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎤᏪᏘ ᏂᏛᏳᎾᏂᎩᏓ ᎥᎾᏛᎦᏅ ᎴᏱᎩ ᏱᎨᏎ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏧᏂᎶᏒ?
segments.translation: Have your parents or grandparents ever told you things that might have happened, coming on the Trail of Tears?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎡᏙᏓᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᏧᎵ ᎨᎵ ᎤᏙᏓ ᎤᏥᎾ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎤᏪᏘ ᏂᏛᏳᎾᏂᎩᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎲᏍ mom’s... ᏏᏉᏯ... ᎤᏂᏙᏗᏍ ᎨᎮ ᎤᏂᏚᏗ ᎨᏍᏊ ᎥᎾ ᏂᏛᏳᏂᎩᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ?
segments.translation: My late dad—both his dad and mom said they came on the Trail of Tears. I think Mom’s… Sigoy… Was it her mom and dad that came from there, too?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᏩᏅᏔᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏂᎵᏏᏭ ᎾᎮᏂ ᏥᎧᏃᎮᏍᎪ ᎤᏲ ᏧᏂᎶᏒ ᎪᎳ ᏱᎩ ᎤᏴᏢ ᏄᎾᏛᏅᏕᎨ ᎠᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᎭᏂ ᎮᏂ ᎥᎾ Sally Bull ᏢᏴ ᏥᎨᎮ ᎥᎾ ᎤᎷᏤ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎬᏯᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎵ ᏚᏙᎡ Ꮎ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎨᏯ ᎥᎾᏅ ᎤᏕᏁ Ꮎ ᏁᏗ ᎤᏕᏅ ᏥᎩᎥᎾ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏁᎸᏕ ᏏᏆᏅ ᎤᏂᎪᏗ ᏚᎾᏢᏁ ᎾᏅ ᎠᏗᏍᎪ ᏙᏩᎴᎶ Ꮲ ᏂᎬᏁ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᏕᎦᏩᏔ ᏱᎩ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎥᎾ ᎤᏞ Ꮎ ᎠᏐᏴ ᏏᏆᏃ ᏒᎯᏰ ᏱᎩ ᎭᎳ ᏛᏎ ᎾᎱᎫᏍᏓᏰ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏯ ᎥᎾ ᎠᏦᏔᏍᎨ ᏝᎦᏭᏅ ᏣᏗᎰ ᏴᏛᎬᎦ ᎨᎮᏃ ᏏᏆᏃ ᎤᎾᏛᎦᏃ ᎮᎾ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎠᏃᏝᎨ ᎠᏂᎦᏐᏏᎯᎰ ᎠᏗᎰ ᎮᏂ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ.
segments.translation: As far as I know it was just their grandma. She used to talk about how bad it was. She said in the winter it was cold. Sometime in the past she came to Sally Bull. I think her name was ‘Gv-Ya-S-Di’, and she lived where Ned lived. And had a lot of pigs, and they said there was something-like-a-wheel-that’s-on-a-car, and she had that in that pen. She must’ve been a loudmouth. And she would blow hard into that. Then in no time [the pigs] would they recognize that [sound], and they would come down the hill, my dad used to say.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏓᏤᏞᏛᎮ ᎤᎾᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ ᏏᏅ ᏗᏂᎳᏫᎦ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Maybe the pigs listen better than church people do.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎣᏍᏛ ᎠᏃᎵᎦ ᎨᎮ ᏏᏆ
segments.translation: The pigs understood good.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛᎭ ᏍᏊ ᏗᎩᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏒᎯᏰᏃ ᎠᎵᏍᏴᏓᏗ ᏱᎩ ᏳᏩᏅᏙ ᎨᎲ ᏙᏯ ᎣᎦᏅᏙ ᏂᏛᏲᎦᏂᎩᏍᏗ
segments.translation: Even our parents used to whoop at us when it was time to eat, and we would come home.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ Ꮎ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ ᏦᏤᎲ ᎯᎢᏅ ᎤᏙᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏈᏍᏓᏅ ᎠᎦᏍᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗᏅ ᏞᏍᏗ ᎤᏟᏴ ᏰᎨᎮ ᎥᎾᏃ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᏕᎦᏃᎱᎩᏍᎬ ᏳᎴᏅ ᎣᎦᏛᏅᏍᏗ ᎮᏃ ᎠᎹᏯ ᏫᏄᎵᏍᏙᏗ ᎡᎵᏍᎨ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᎹᏯ ᏳᏄᎵᏍᏛᏁ ᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏄᎸᎲᏍᎬ ᏭᏛᎾᏫᏗ ᏱᏙᏛᏍᏛᏲᎯ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏒᏕᏂ ᎬᏗ ᏃᏭ ᎣᎦᏛᏅᏍᏗ ᎤᏚᎵᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏱᎩᎬᎦᏍᎩ ᎣᏣᏂᎩᏍᎪ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ Ꮎ ᏬᎩᏒᎯᎰ
segments.translation: I remember when we used to live down by the creek and this One’s [Jerry’s] dad—it used to rain a lot, and the school wasn’t too far and used to flood. His dad would be ready for us to move. It came close a few times, but it never did. He would fire off a shotgun when he wanted us to leave. And, sometimes it would be pouring down rain and we would get up and move, and spend the night at school.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᎾ Star of BethlehemᎢ ᏥᎦᏗ
segments.translation: Where the Star of Bethlehem [church] is.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎮᏂ ᏥᎦᏗᏍᎬ ᎩᎳ ᏫᏳᏍᏗ ᎡᏘᏴ ᎮᏂ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᏛᏩᏍᎬ ᏗᏕᎳᏆᏍᏗ ᎤᏛᎴᎾᏗ ᎾᏂᎨᏍᏗ ᎤᏴᎸᏂ ᏣᏂᏃᏟᏍᏗᎰ Ꮓ ᎠᎴᎾᏗ ᏱᎩᏃᎴ ᎤᏴᎸᏂ ᏣᏂᏃᏟᏍᏗᎰ
segments.translation: Like I was saying, a little bit ago—when it was almost time for Sunday school, they would ring a bell. Then when it was time for church, they would ring it again.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᏛᎭ Ꮟ ᏍᎩ ᏂᏛᏛᏁᎰ
segments.translation: We still do that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏅᏛᎩᏍᎨ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏂᏴᏫ Ꮓ ᏥᏗᎾᎢᏐ
segments.translation: People would hear it, and would start coming in.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎩᎶᏛ ᏍᏊ ᏳᎪᎶᏏ ᎨᎮ SalemᎢ ᎥᎾ ᎮᏂ ᎣᏣᏕᎳᎰᏍᎬ ᎩᎶ ᏃᎦᏛᏂ ᏧᏃᏴᎬ ᎯᎸᏍᎩᎢ ᎮᏂ ᏗᏎᏢᏗ Ꭴ ᎪᏃᏟᏍᏗᎲ ᏲᎮᏂ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎪᎯᎦ Ꭷ ᏗᏣᏍᏆᎸᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎤᏃᏴᎦ ᎨᎲ ᎤᏯᎸᏂ ᎩᎶ ᎮᏂ ᏦᎩᏃᏍᎩᏒ ᎥᎾ. ᎾᎯᏳᏃ Ꮲ ᏱᎬᏴᏛᎦ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏍᎩᏂ Ᏺ ᏴᏛᎦᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ Ꮎ ᏧᏯᎸᏂ
segments.translation: Even when someone passes away at Salem, they count and ring it a few times. Back then that bell used to really sound good, but somebody stole it from us. Now we don’t really do it no more. But back then we could hear it good.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᏥᏥᏁᎸ ᏣᏩᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᎦᎵᏉᎦ Ᏼ ᏳᏟᎶᏓ ᏥᏛᏓᏁᎸ ᏦᎩᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎣᏣᏛᎩᏍᎬᏛ ᎤᏃᏴᎬ ᏃᎴ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏚᏃᏴᎬ “Ꮒ ᎩᎶ ᏛᎭ ᏁᎲᎾ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏓ” ᏣᎾᏗᏍᎪᏃ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏣᎾᏁᎷᎩᏍᎪ ᎦᎲ ᏳᏍᏓ? ᏧᏭᏂᎦᏛᎲᏍᎪ ᎦᎦ ᎨᎲ. ᏍᎩᏛᎮ ᏂᏨᏛᏁ ᎨᎮ ᏙᎲ ᏱᏧᏃᏴᎵᏌ ᎢᏣᏁᎷᎩᏍᎨ
segments.translation: I remember when we lived in town, growing up, and we lived about seven miles from the church. And we could hear the ring. Sometimes it would ring a long time, and they would say, “Look someone passed away.” Some would rush over there and see who passed. Is that what y’all used to do when y’all heard it—you’d rush over there?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏅᏛᎭᏲ ᎠᏂᏍᎪᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎾᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᏍᏓᏯ ᏚᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ
segments.translation: Back then they would dig the grave. They would work hard.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎤᎵᏨᏛᏩᏗᏛ ᏣᎾᏍᎪᏍᎪ ᏗᎨᎬ ᏗᏢ ᏍᏊ ᎪᎳ ᏱᎩ ᎠᏫᏴ ᏧᏃᏙ ᎧᏫ ᎢᏃ ᏧᏂᎦᎣ ᎯᎾ ᏗᏢ ᏣᎾᏍᎪᏍᎪ
segments.translation: They would dig all night, even in the wintertime, where I come from. They would have a fire close by, and coffee brewing.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏯᏅᏛᏁ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ SalemᎢ ᎠᎾᏍᎪᏍᎩ. ᎠᎩᏙᏓᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎯᏯᏛ ᏑᏓᎵ ᎯᏍᎩᏛ ᏍᏗ ᎤᎶᏒᏍᏗ ᏍᏗ ᏂᎦᏗ ᏯᏂᏯᎥᎩ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎾᏟᎶᏍᎬ. ᎠᏂᎨ ᎡᏲ ᎤᎾᏕᏃ ᎨᎲ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎡᎳᏓ ᏥᏗᏓᏁᎵ ᎥᎾ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎰ ᎥᎾᎵᏍᏓᏗ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏗᏢ ᎡᎲ ᏌᏭ. ᎡᏚᏥ ᏛᎮ ᏴᎪᏏ ᎨᎲ John Acorn ᎥᎾ ᎮᎢ ᎠᏯ ᎡᏥ ᏗᎾᏓᎸ ᎠᏂᏁᎸ Ꮭ ᎩᎶ ᏱᎦᏥᏃᎯᏏ ᎡᏚᏥ ᏥᏲᏎᎲ ᏚᏳᎦᏛ ᏌᏚ ᎠᏰᏟᏢ ᏯᏅᎷᏓᏂᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏛᏅ ᎢᎦ ᏓᏁᏠᎲ Ꮎ ᏧᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎯ ᏍᏭ ᎠᏯᏙᎯ ᏙᏳ ᏧᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁ ᎤᏟ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏛᏂᎩᏍᎬ ᎥᎾ ᎠᏯᎡ ᏣᎾᏗᎲ ᎬᏂᎮ ᏅᏱ ᎤᎦᏔᏂᏞ ᏍᎩᎾᏅ john ᏙᏳ ᏛᏍᏊ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗ ᎤᏛᏁ ᏣᎾᏗᎲ ᏱᎾᎦᎵᏍᏗ ᏂᎬᏁᎡ
segments.translation: That’s what they used to do, at Salem, was dig. My dad was just a little over five feet tall. They would put him in there to see how deep it was. The women brought lunches though. That house-that-was-on-the-bottom—that was where we ate. There was that One who lived down below. He was my uncle, John Acorn. He was married to my mom’s sister. I wouldn’t tell anybody he was my uncle. He was show up around 11:30 [am] because he knew they served the workers’ lunch. There was one deacon, he was a hard worker, and he was from a long way away. He got down in there [digging] and he hit a rock. John peeked in and he said, “It’s really getting done ain’t it?” And the deacon says, “It’s not getting done, I’m getting it done.”

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎾᎾᎭ ᎠᏂᏰᏫᏒᏍᎩ ᏣᏁᎲ, ᏍᏊᏍ ᎠᏁᎯ ᏏᎨ ᎸᏢ ᏃᏭ?
segments.translation: What about the ones who sew, are there still any alive?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᏯᏁᎯ
segments.translation: There ain’t hardly any still alive.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ SalemᎢ ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏯᏅᏛᏁ ᎨᎲ ᎯᎸᏍᎩ ᏯᏂ ᎠᏂᎨᏯ ᏯᏁᏂ
segments.translation: That’s what the women used to do at Salem.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎡᎳᏗ ᎾᏍᏊ. Mama ᏥᎨᎲ pieᎢ ᎮᏂ ᏌᏭ ᏔᎵ ᎴᏱᎩ ᏱᏕᎪᎸᏂ ᎨᎲ ᏥᏔᎩᏅ ᏯᏒᏂᏛᎩ ᎥᎾ ᎦᏚ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏃᏅ rag ᏱᏓᎧᏁᎩ ᎦᏚ ᎪᎯᏅᏍᏗ ᎡᎳᏗᏅ
segments.translation: They used to go on foot. Mama would make one or two pies, and fried chicken. She would tie a rag to carry it on foot.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎡᎳᏗ yeah. ᏙᎮᏂ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎾᎾᏛᏁ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏣᏩᏛᏏᏗᏒ ᏥᏧᏣ ᎡᏥ ᏥᏍᏓᏩᏕᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᏦᎢᏁ ᎢᎦᏛ ᎨᎵ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: On foot, yeah. That’s what they used to do when I was a little boy. Growing up, I would go with Mom on Wednesdays to church.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏣᏅᏔ ᏙᎯᏳ ᏣᎵᏍᏓᏱᏗ
segments.translation: You knew you were really going to eat then.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Yeah, ᎤᏬᏟᏗ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎰ ᎠᏂᏰᏫᏍᎪ. ᎯᏛᎭ ᏄᏍᏓ ᎠᎾᏗᎰᏛ ᏃᏛ ᎠᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ ᏥᎨᎰ ᎯᏛ ᏥᏄᏛᏁᎶ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᏂᏰᏩᏏᏍᎪᏛ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏍᎪ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎤᏬᏟᏗᏛ ᎤᏂᏰᎸᏐ.
segments.translation: Yeah. It was funny what they would do when they would sew. They would say, “This is how it goes,” while they were sewing. They would talk about anything funny.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏙᏗ ᎠᏂᏰᏫᏒᏍᎩᏗᏛ ᎠᏁᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, they were some real sewers back then.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᏂᎾᏕᎪᏛ ᎨᎲ ᏰᎦᏟ ᏍᎩᎾ WMU Ꭷ ᏧᎾᏙᏢᏒ ᎾᎯᏳ
segments.translation: They would sell quilts. They had a group called WMU [Woman’s (Baptist) Missionary Union] back then.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᏧᏬᏚ ᏓᏂᏰᏫᏒᏍᎬ ᎾᎯᏳ
segments.translation: They made them really pretty, back then.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎤᏬᏚᎯ ᏂᏓᏅᏁᎰ
segments.translation: They made them real pretty.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: yeah, ᎡᏍᏙᎵᎦᏛ ᎨᎮ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎠᎦᏘᏂᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ Woody Hair ᏧᏙᎢᏓ. ᎭᏢ ᏙᏘᎳᏫᏤᏏ ᏳᏛᏂ ᎥᎾ ᏤᏣᏯᏂᎢ SalemᎢᏛ ᏩᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᏓᏁᏏᏛ ᎠᏬᏎᎰ
segments.translation: Do you two know Woody Hair? Sometimes he used to take me around. He would say, “Where are they calling you?” I would say, “Salem,” and he would say, “We’re going.”

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏧᏲᎱᏒᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎤᎸᏉᏗ ᏥᎨᏒ
segments.translation: He liked Belfonte, too.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏏᏍ ᎡᎯ Woody?
segments.translation: Is Woody still alive?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏧᏲᎱᏒ
segments.translation: He passed away.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎤᏲᎱᏎᏕ
segments.translation: Oh, he passed away?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎮᏂ ᎭᏢᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏦᏍᏕᏛᎲ... ᎠᏯᏛᏃ ᎮᏍᏗ ᏱᏥᏍᎦᏯᎭ ᎠᎩᏲᎱᎯᏍᏗ ᎤᏛᏅ “alright praise the lord” ᎠᏩᏛᏅ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎾᎮ ᏂᎬᏁᎵᏓ ᏱᎩ ᎨᎵᎰᏛ. ᏚᏂᏨᏍᏙ ᎮᏂ ᏧᎾᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᎤᏛᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏩᏅᏔᏛ ᏛᏩᏂᎩᏒ SalemᎢ ᏥᏈᏍᏓ ᏥᏓᏨᏍᏛ ᏧᎾᏓᏂᏐᏗ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏯᏅᏛᏛ Woody ᎤᏬᏟᏓᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ.
segments.translation: One time... where were we at? Woody said, “I ain’t afraid to die anymore.” I said, “Alright praise the Lord.” I guess he got right. Woody said, “They got lights on now at the cemetery.” That’s what reminded me of him, when I drove by that Salem Church—seeing a lot of lights was Woody. He was funny.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᎬᏱᏛᏅ Totem Hair ᏥᏲᎵᎦ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᏗᎦᏘᏍᏗ ᏗᎪᏢᏍᎩ ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎦᏪᏟᏍᎦ ᎨᎲ ᏍᏊ. ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ ᏗᎦᏘᏍᏓ Ꮎ ᎣᏍᏓᏢᏅᏢ Ꮎ Martin ᎣᎩᏂᎷᏨ ᏗᎦᏘᏍᏗ ᏧᏩᏏᏢ ᎨᎲ ᏕᎪᏢᏍᎬ boy this one oughta be a good one ᎤᏛᏅ oughta be fast. ᏙᎨ? FordᏅ spring ᏳᎵᏍᏓᏅ ᎢᎦ ᎤᏛᏅ ᏢᏍ ᏯᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏳᏰᏟᏗ ᏦᏍᏗᏬᏂ ᏗᎨᏲᏗ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ.
segments.translation: I first knew Totem Hair. He made [fishing] gigs. He used to joke around, too, while he was making gigs. My brother Martin used to buy gigs from him. He said, “Boy this one ought to be a good one, it ought to be fast.” “Why’s that?” “It’s made with a spring from a Ford.” You could barely catch it. I don’t know if us talking is suitable for children.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏗ ᎤᏃᏟᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ.
segments.translation: They were really funny.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᏍᏊᏅ ᏗᎦᏣᏃᏍᏗᏭ ᏥᎨᎰ ᏗᎦᏘᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏩᎩᎸᏉᏛ ᏣᏗᎲ Ꮎ Ꮭ ᏯᏂᏯ Redhorse ᎠᎭᏂᏛ ᏗᏢ ᏅᏯ ᏳᏓᏩᏗᎾ ᏣᏗᎲᏃ ᏣᏅᏗᏢᎢᏐ ᏃᏭ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏩᎩᎸᏉᏓ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏱᏥᏯᏘᏟ ᏌᏭ ᎠᏫ ᏫᏥᏌᎳᏗᏍᎪᏛ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎯᏍᎩᎭ ᏑᏓᎵᎭ ᎩᎳ ᏱᏗᏥᏩᏛᏅ. ᎩᎳ ᏥᎾᏒᏁᏍᎬ. ᏙᏳᏛ ᎧᏃᎮᏢᏍᎩ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎣᏍᏗᏩᏛᎮᎬ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎣᏍᏓᏛᏓᏍᏙᏗ ᎠᎸᎯᏳ
segments.translation: “And I like those straight gigs, they’re my favorite,” he said. “If there’s a place that has those redhorses, we would throw rocks and they would come out and I would stick them. I wouldn’t pull my gig up until I had five or six on there,” he said. He was a real storyteller. We would go see him, just to listen to him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Radio Wilson ᏧᏙᎢᏓ ᏤᎲ ᎾᏍᎩᏯ ᏧᎦᎸᏗ ᎠᏑᏂᏙ ᏛᎨᎲ ᎤᏢᎦᏩᏒᏗ ᏗᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎨᎲ. ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏗ ᎠᎦᏑᏅᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᎠᏤ ᎠᎩᏩᏒ ᏗᏑᏗ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏃᎴ ᏓᏪᏘᏅᏛ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎥᎾ ᎠᏩᎵᏍᏛᏡᏅ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎠᏩᏍᎩᎸ ᎠᏩᎵᏍᏚᏢᏍᏗ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎠᏭᏴ ᎮᏂ ᏂᏧᎵᏍᏓᏂ ᎦᏐᏩᎸ ᎬᏗ ᏥᎨᎰ. ᏍᎩᎾᏃ ᎦᏕᎳᎰᏍᎪ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏗ Ꮎ ᎢᏤ ᎠᎩᏩᏒ ᏑᏗ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏧᎵᏍᏛᏅ ᎠᎹᏯ ᏭᏕᎵᏍᎬ ᏣᏗᎲ boy ᏃᏛᎭ ᎠᎩᏴᎡ ᎢᏤ Ꮭ ᏍᏊ ᏱᏛᎩᏴᎡᎵ ᎠᏪᎵᏒ ᏩᏮᏕᏘᏅᏛ ᏥᎨᎲᏒ ᎠᎹᏯ ᎭᏫᎾ ᏥᎨᎯᏙᎰ ᏗᏑᏗ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎠᏣᏗ ᎥᎾᎾ ᏃᏍᏊ ᏓᎩᏯᏍᎪ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎭᏫᎾ ᏗᏢ ᏙᏩᎴᎳ ᎤᏪᏘ ᏛᎫᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏭᏣᏅ ᎠᏣᏗ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏑᏗ ᎦᏁᎯ ᏙᏚᏒᎳᏓᏅ ᏗᏦᎸᏂ. ᏙᎯᏳ ᏧᎦᎸᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: Radio Wilson was a fisher, too. And he bragged a lot. “One time, I went fishing,” he said. “I bought a brand-new fishing pole, and I stood it up and sat back. I was fishing and I saw the bobber go under. It jerked my fishing pole so hard, and [the pole] started to go in after the bobber,” he said. “I’m not going to let it take my new fishing pole,” he thought, and went in the water, chasing after his fishing pole. “There was an old car down there, and the fish went inside the car and rolled the windows up,” he said. He was really ornery.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏛᎭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏛᏰᏣᎨᎯᏙᎵ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏫᏙᎯᏃᏎᎸ ᏦᏥᏬᏂ
segments.translation: For that reason, they’re going to run you off, if you tell the kids what we’re talking about.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎰᏩᏅ ᎣᏤᎵᎲ
segments.translation: And we really believe it!

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏃᎴ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏗ Ꮯounty ᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ lake ᎢᎾᎠ ᏙᏣᎵᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎬ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏩ ᎤᏛᏠᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ Radio. “Where you going radio?” “Going fishing.” “you been catching here lately?” “Yeah, boy I caught a big one!”, ᎤᏛᏅ. “That big!” “How much did it weigh?” ᎠᎪᏎᎸ. “Well, picture alone weighed five pounds!”
segments.translation: One time when I was working for the County at the lake. We were on a lunch break, and Radio showed up. I asked, “Where you going, Radio?” “I’m going fishing,” he said. “You been catching anything lately?” “Oh yeah, boy I caught a big one, ‘that’ big,” he said. “How much did it weigh?” I said to him, “Well, picture alone weighed five pounds.”

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏙᎲ ᎡᏆ ᎠᏥᏂᏴᎮ
segments.translation: He really caught a big one, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎤᏨᏛᏅ ᏛᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ. ᏓᏂᏂᏗᎲ ᏥᏗᏃᎮ
segments.translation: Yeah, he was the best. Oh, they’re recording what we’re saying!

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎩᎳ ᏩᏕᎳᎰ
segments.translation: He just now figured it out!

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᎣᎦᏚᎵᏍᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎧᏃᎮᏗ. ᎤᏬᏟᏗ ᎾᏍᏊ
segments.translation: That’s what we wanted—good stories. Funny, too.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ ᏍᏊ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏥᎩ ᏃᏭ. ᏱᏂᎦᏛᏂ ᏦᎳ ᏳᎾᏍᎬᏝᏅᏃ ᏛᏲ ᏛᏰᏣᏛᏅᏂ. ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᏓᎦᏘᏰ ᏁᎲᏂ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ
segments.translation: Well, my brother-that’s-passed, when he’d stick tobacco in his mouth, you knew he was going to tell you stories. He was a pastor at Belfonte.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Oh, Ꮎ Martin?
segments.translation: Oh, was it Martin?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎥᎲ, ᎣᏂ ᎮᏂ Tom. MartinᎡ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏚᎦᏘᏛ
segments.translation: No, Tom was last. Martin was before him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎯᏳᏛ ᏝᎦ ᏧᏩᏪᏙᎸ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ Tom ᏁᎲᏂ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ. ᏢᏛᎮ ᏔᎵᏁ ᏱᏅᏓ ᏳᏩᏪᏙᎵ ᏦᎢᏅᏓ ᎴᏱᎩᏃ ᎣᏂ ᏧᏭᎷᏨ McLemore ᏧᏙᎢᏓ ᏥᎩ ᎠᏧᏣ
segments.translation: It was about that time when I was going to Belfonte for a little while, when Tom passed away. About the second time I went there, for three months, a McLemore boy arrived there.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎾᏛ Martin, thirty-two years ᎨᎵ ᏗᎦᏘᏱᏛ
segments.translation: Martin preached for 32 years, I think.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: yeah, ᎪᎯᎦ ᏚᎦᏘᏛ
segments.translation: Yeah, he preached for a long time.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: TomᎢᏅ ᎦᎵᏉᎩ. ᏂᎯᎨᏃ ᎤᎾᏛᏅ. ᏯᏂᏅᎪᏨᏂᏛᎮ ᎠᏯ ᏳᏩᎩᏬᏂᏒ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎸ
segments.translation: Tom was there for seven. “How about you?” they said. I told them, “Everyone would walk out if I spoke.”

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: TomᎢᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᎮᏂ ᎤᏬᏟᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏴᏫ ᎨᎲ ᎾᏛ ᎠᏮᎨᏩᏌᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎭᏢ ᏭᎵᏥᏙᏅ Ꮎ
segments.translation: Tom was a really funny person. Somewhere… I forget where he preached at--

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏣᎳᎩ ᎤᏪᏘ
segments.translation: --North Carolina--

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏣᎳᎩ ᎤᏪᏘ ᏕᎨᏥᏯᏗ ᏧᏛᏅ
segments.translation: --North Carolina. “I told them some things,” he said.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎾᏛ Norman West ᏧᏘᏅᏒ ᏙᎲ. ᎦᎯᎵᏥᏙᎾᏏᏍ ᏧᏃᎮᎸ. ᎥᎥ ᏫᏕᎦᏥᏯᏘᏛ ᏧᏛᏅ
segments.translation: It was Norman West that took him, ain’t it? They asked him, “Did you preach to them?” And he said, “Yeah, I told them some things.”

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎯᏲᎵᎦᏍ ᎨᎮ Ꮎ Norman West?
segments.translation: Did you know Norman West?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏱᎨᎵ ᏥᎪᎥ ᎴᏱᎦ
segments.translation: I don’t think so, but maybe I’ve seen him.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏧᎦᎸᏗᏛ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: He was ornery.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: yeah, ᎠᏭ ᎮᏂᏴ ᏗᎦᎾᏗᏫᏒ ᏅᏃ ᏥᎬᏁᎸ ᏥᏥᏁᎵ ᎠᏯ
segments.translation: Yeah, he lived just across the road from where I lived.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: Ꮎ Emmanuel ᏣᏃᎮ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ ᎥᎾ ᎤᎴᏅᎲ ᎪᎯᎩᏴ ᏍᎩᎾ
segments.translation: It was at the church they call ‘Emmanuel’—that’s where he started a long time ago.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ ᏥᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏍᏊ Tom ᏥᏙᏣᏏᏛᏛ ᏥᏯᏅᏛᏗᏍᎪᏛ. ᎣᎩᎾᎵ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅᏃ ᎾᎯᏳᏃ Tom ᏥᏲᎵᎦ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏅ.
segments.translation: I took part in the work when we laid hands on him and ordained him. I remember him. We became friends after I got to know him.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎾᏛ Woody ᏙᎯᏳ ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾᎵ ᏥᎨᎲᏓᎦᏂᏰᎪᎦ ᎤᎴ ᏱᎨᎮ
segments.translation: Him and Woody were real good friends, too. They both lied just as much.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏂᎬᏭ ᏙᎲ ᎠᏃᎵᎦ ᎨᎮ Woody ᎭᏢᏭ ᏳᏬᎩᏂᎷᏥ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎠᎭᏂᏧ ᏔᎵᏥᏙᏁᏌ ᏴᏬᏎᎳ ᎠᎭᏂᏛ ᏗᏢ ᏩᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᏓᏁᏏᏛ ᏛᎬᏯᏘᏅᏍᏛᏂ ᎠᏗᏍᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᎦᏳᎳ ᎠᎪᎵᎦ ᎡᎨᎰ ᏳᏬᎩᏂᎷᏣ ᎥᎾ
segments.translation: I guess they knew Woody everywhere. He would ask me, “Where are you going?” and I would say, “I’m going this way,” and he would say, “I’m going to take you, we’re going together.” They already knew him everywhere he went.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: Ꮎ ᏍᎪᏂᏲ Ꮎ ᎠᎨᏯ Ꮟ ᎡᎯᏲ ᏢᎨ
segments.translation: Is That Woman still alive?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: yeah, ᎡᎱᏛ
segments.translation: Yeah, she’s still alive.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏙᏳ Ꮕ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏂᎪᎸ ᎤᎾᎵᎪ ᎨᎲ ᏙᎲ
segments.translation: They went everywhere together, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏧᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ Kenwood ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎲ ᎩᎶ ᏗᏛᏛᏁ ᏗᎾᏕᎳᏆᏍᎩ ᏣᏗᎲ “Who's the father of our country?” ᎤᏛᏁ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏗᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩᏅ “Who?” “Woody Hair!” ᎤᏛᏁ ᏂᎬᏅ ᎠᏁᎮ ᏧᏪᏣ. ᏗᏍᏗᎪᎵᏰᏍᎩᏍ ᏣᎳᎩ ᏗᎪᏪᎳ?
segments.translation: Yeah. One time at Kenwood School someone told me the students were asked, “Who’s the father of our country? Who?” “Woody Hair!” they said. His kids were everywhere. Do you two read Cherokee?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎲᎥ
segments.translation: No.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏝᎩ
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᏰ ᎠᎮ ᏭᎪᏛ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎣᏍᏗᏬᏂᏍᎦ ᎠᎮᏅ Ꮲ ᏦᏍᏗᎪᎵᏰᏍᎦ ᏱᎦ. ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ Ꮲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗᏯ ᎩᏄᎸᏂ ᎯᎢ ᎮᏂ ᏫᏥᏴᏓᏁᎰ. ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎰ Ꮎ ᎠᏯ ᏨᎩᎵᏌ Ꮟ ᏤᎱᏭ ᎮᏂᎵ ᎡᏣᎵᏃᎮᏙᏗ ᎠᏯ ᏥᏍᎩᏯᏛᏛᎲᏍᎪ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏅᏩᏛᏂ ᏲᎮᏂ ᎥᎾᏙ ᎮᏂ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᏥᏲᎮᎰ ᎠᏎᎾ ᎢᎦᏛ ᎠᏂᏍᎫᏓᏍᏓᏯ ᎾᏛ ᏧᎾᏝᏃᎮᏗ ᏱᏓᏂᎯᏙ ᎡᎦ ᏌᏭ Ꮎ ᎤᏔᏂᏓᏲ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏝᏂᎬᏁ ᏍᏊᎮᎢ ᏱᏂᏣᏪᏌ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎬᏗ ᏲᎮᏂ ᏱᎪᏪᎸᎦ ᎭᎸᏍᎩᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏳᏒ ᏱᏯᏛᏛᏂ ᏱᏣᏃᎯᏏ ᏯᏛᏗ ᏳᏄᎸᎲᏍᎩᎾ ᎩᎶᏫ ᏱᎪᎯᏓ ᏯᏩᏗ. ᏍᎩᎮᏂᏅ Arkansas ᏫᏓᏕᎳᏆ ᏚᏍᏆᏗᏓ
segments.translation: We probably speak mostly Cherokee, but we can’t read it. If I don’t know something, I call him [Henry]. That’s what my grandkids tell me, “While Henry is still alive you need to talk to him instead of asking me about things I don’t know.” That’s what I tell them, but they’re real hardheaded. The oldest one is really trying hard. If you say something in Cherokee, he’ll write it down and, a few days later, he can still say it. If he can’t, he can find it really quick. That’s the one that’s going to the University of Arkansas. I think he lacks just a little bit being done [is almost finished studying].

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏢᎮ ᎠᏂᏣᎳᎩ ᎠᏂᏬᏂᏍᏈ ᏗᏍᏓᏓᎵᏌ ᏗᏍᏕᏣ ᎴᏱᎩ
segments.translation: So, you two don’t have any grandkids, or kids, that speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏱᏗ ᏛᎮ ᎤᏩᏌ ᏯᏃᎵᎩ. ᏙᏳᏛ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎠᏝᏂᎬᏁ. ᎠᎨᏳᏥᏅ ᎾᏛ ᎠᏯ ᎠᏪᏣ ᏁᎲᎾ ᏥᏂᎦᎵᏍᏓ ᏥᎬᏗᎲ ᎡᎵᏲ ᎪᎵᎬ ᏙᎲ
segments.translation: “It’s time to eat,” is the only thing they understand. He really is the only one that is trying. That Girl, the daughter-of-my-son-that-passed-away, she understood and spoke it a little bit, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎥᎥ, ᏲᏛᏲ ᎪᎵᎬ
segments.translation: Yeah, she understood.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᎬᏬᏂᏍᎬᏅ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎩᎾᏴ ᏥᏂᎦᏛ mom ᎤᎦᏘᏗᏍᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎭ
segments.translation: When she was about [gestures] tall Mom would watch after her, all in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏣᎳᎩᎭ
segments.translation: All Cherokee.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: MomᎢ ᎮᎾ Ꮭ ᏲᏁᎦ ᎬᏬᏂᏍᎦ ᏱᎨᎮ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏂᏐ ᎠᏂᏥᏣ ᏳᎵᎪ Mom ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏚᏬᎮᎳ ᏂᎴ ᏚᏃᏎᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏄᏪᏒ Mom ᏙᏛᎮᏲ ᎧᎵ ᎪᎵᎨ
segments.translation: Mom didn’t speak English. So, when she was with the other boys, and Mom would say something, That Girl would turn to the other boys and tell them what she said. That Girl fully understood.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏍ ᎥᎲ, ᎾᎾ ᎡᏘᏴ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎩᏗ ᎤᏂᎪᎲ ᎠᎴ ᎤᏅᏛᎦᏅ Ꮲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎨᏍᏗᏃᏎᎸ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎢᎦᏕ ᏭᏂᎪᏛ ᎨᎲ ᏴᏩ ᏧᎾᏍᏗ ᏓᏂᏃᎮᏍᎪ.
segments.translation: Ain’t it, yeah. What about, a long time ago, did they ever tell you anything interesting or strange they saw or heard? Like for instance, little people.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: Ꮒ ᏛᎭᏲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏥᎪᎥ ᏗᏤᏅᎲ ᎾᎠ
segments.translation: I did see something by your house [Henry].

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎥᎥ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏛᏲ ᏥᎪᎥ
segments.translation: Yeah, I saw something, too.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: Ꮩ ᎠᏫᏄᏣ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: When I was a teenager.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎾᎮᏂ Bigfoot ᏣᎾᏗᏍᎪ ᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏄᏛᏁᎸ ᎤᏓᎾᏫᏍᏛᎾ ᏅᏃ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏪᏘ ᏫᎦᏅᏅ ᎥᎾ Fog Holler
segments.translation: I don’t know what it was, but it looked like what they call ‘Bigfoot’, going down the road by Fog Holler.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: Dirt road.
segments.translation: Dirt road.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: Dirt road, ᎥᎾ ᏥᏍᏚ ᎮᏂ ᏕᏥᎠᎷᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ ᏒᎯᏰ ᏱᎩᎾ ᏣᎾᏓᏅᏍᎪ ᎪᏍᏚ ᏱᎩᏥᏙᎪ ᏅᏃᎱᏟᏗ. ᏱᎬᎩᎪᏩᏘᏩ ᏍᏊ Ꮲ ᎮᏂ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏱᎦᎷᎨ ᎥᎾ ᎤᏙᏛᎴᏒ ᏳᏍᏓ ᎥᎾ ᏧᏍᏏ ᏚᏩᏯᏢ ᎥᎾ ᏭᏟᏗᏢ ᏥᏙᎪ ᏩᏩᎦᏎᏍᏙ ᎠᏩ ᎤᏟ ᏗᏢᏴ ᏛᏰᎲ ᎠᏧᏣ Teehee ᎠᏧᏣ ᎠᎩᏩᏛᎯᏙ ᎨᎲ. ᏍᏊᏭᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏩᏓᏅᏖᏢ ᏄᎦᏐᏒ ᎮᏂ ᏅᏃ ᎢᎾᎦ ᏂᏛᏳᎶᏒ ᎥᎾ ᏭᎦᏓ ᏍᏊᏭᏅ ᏩᏩᏓᏅᏖᏢ ᎠᎮᏅ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ. ᏄᎴᏫᏍᏓᏂᏅ ᎥᎾ
segments.translation: Dirt road. ’Cause, late in the evening, I used to wait for rabbits when they were in the dust. But maybe they seen me, because they weren’t moving around. I was standing up against a dirt embankment with branches. I was standing on the other side of that, and I was watching. And, way over there, was a boy, a Teehee boy. He used to come to visit me sometimes. That is what I thought of. When I saw him come off the hill from the woods to the road, that’s what I thought of.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: Boy ᎨᏯᏔᎯ ᏛᏎ ᏲᎨᎲ ᎠᏫᏅ ᏂᎬᏩᏍᏛ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎠᏍᎪᎵ ᏫᏚᎾᏗᏒ ᏅᏃ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎤᏍᏓ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎮᏂ ᎢᎩᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎭᏂᏅ ᎨᎲ Ꮓ ᎮᏍᏓ ᎧᏴᏤᏂ ᏳᏙᏢᏎᏃ ᏱᏂᎬᏩᏍᏕ ᏙᎮᏂ ᎠᏝᎲᏭ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏍᎪᎵ. ᎤᎵᏏᎦ ᎮᏂ ᏲᎨᎲ ᎲᏅ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᎤᏭᏯᏖ ᏛᎮ. ᏛᎬᏅᎪᎬ ᎥᎾ ᎨᏓᎵ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᎩᎶᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᎠᏁᏙᎲ Ꮎ ᏏᏆ ᏒᎯᏰ ᎩᎶᏭᏅ ᏭᏕᎵᏧ ᎠᎭᏂ Ꮓ ᏌᎷᏯ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏧᏣᏲᏍᏗ ᎩᎶᎡᏴ ᏭᎶᏒ Ꮎ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ. ᎩᎶ ᏭᏕᎵᏨ ᏏᏆ ᏄᏂᏍᎦᏍᏛᏅ ᎠᏯ ᏍᏊ ᏩᏮᏠᏒ ᏅᏃ ᏩᏮᏓᎾᏮᏍᏛᏅ ᏓᏁᎸ ᏗᏢ
segments.translation: Boy, he looked like something wild. This [gestures] is how he did his head. Then he crossed the road, and looked like he didn’t have a neck. Like it [his head] was just sitting there. It was dark, I think he had fur. Mom had a place downhill to wash clothes, and he disappeared that way. It was thick and had stickers, and he went right through there, and scared those pigs. And I got down, and ran down the hill towards the house.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏍᏊ ᎠᎦᏍᎦᏍᏛᏅ ᏙᎲ
segments.translation: It scared him, too, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎭᎴᏅ ᏕᎬᎩᎪᏅᎲᏩᏅ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏏᏆ. ᎣᏂ ᏗᏢ ᎠᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ. ᎦᎸᎸᏗ ᎤᏓᏒᎳᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ. ᎥᎾ ᎤᏂᏴᏟᏢ Ꮎ ᏏᏆ
segments.translation: The pigs beat me back to the house. The house was raised off the ground, in the back towards the kitchen, and those pigs went underneath the house.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎭᏫᎾ?
segments.translation: Underneath?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎥᎥ, ᏙᎲ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎤᏂᏍᎦᏍᏓᏏ Ꮎ ᏏᏆ ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ? Ꮫ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂ Ꭸ ᏥᏂᏕᎦᎾᏗ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎥᎾᏅ Ꮲ ᎠᏂᎪᏩᏗ ᏗᎬᏅᎪᎬ ᏗᏢ ᏢᏅ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah. Dad asked me, “What scared the pigs?” “I don’t know, but something crossed the road, and they saw it over there by the spring. I don’t know what it was.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎲ ᎤᏂᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎴ ᏏᏆ ᏱᎬᏩᎦᏓ ᏙᎲ
segments.translation: It even scared the pigs, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏲᎮᏂᏲ ᏍᎩᎾ Bigfoot ᎰᏩ ᎾᏁᎵᏍᎬᎾ ᏥᎨᎰ. Ꮲ ᎮᏂ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ Bigfoot ᏱᎩ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎮᏂᏲ ᏥᎪᎥ
segments.translation: Some people believe in Bigfoot. I don’t know if it was Bigfoot, but I saw something.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏛᎭ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏱᏗᎧᏃᏎᎳ Ꮲ ᎰᏩ ᏱᎬᏁᎳ
segments.translation: If you tell some people that, they won’t believe it.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎲᎥ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗᏛᏲ ᎡᎭ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎮᏂ
segments.translation: No, but there is something in the woods, though.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: yeah, ᎡᎯᏛ. ᎮᏍᏗ Ꮫ ᏱᎦᏓ ᏳᏍᏓ ᎡᎲ ᎢᎾᎨ
segments.translation: Yeah, it lives there. We don’t know what all lives in the woods.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎲᏍ ᏱᎧᏁᏍᏗ ᎪᏪᎵ? ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏓ
segments.translation: Does it talk about that in the Bible?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: well, ᎠᏣᎳᎩᎡ ᎨᎲ ᎨᎵ ᎪᏪᎳ ᏴᏫ ᏳᏪᏘ ᎠᎾᏗ ᏴᏫ ᏳᏪᏘ ᎠᎾᏗ
segments.translation: Well, in the Cherokee Bible. I think it’s written, a ‘mythical being’ they said.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᏙᎩ ᎤᏍᏗ?
segments.translation: What did you say?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏴᏫ ᎤᏪᏘ ᎠᎾᏗ. ᏙᎮᏂ ᎢᎾᎨ ᎡᏙ. ᎡᎵᏏ ᎮᏂ ᏍᏊ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏭ ᏨᎫᎳ ᏗᏢ ᏥᏧᏣ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏌᏭᏅ ᎤᏪᏣ ᏙᏗ ᏴᏗ ᎡᏚᏥᏛ ᏚᏓᏘᎾᎥ ᏣᏁᎬ ᎠᏂ ᎤᏛᎯᏍᏗ ᎾᏂᎨᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ Ꮎ ᏠᎨᏌ ᏚᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎥᎾᏛ ᏱᏤᎾ ᏱᏥᏃᎯᏌ ᎠᎩᎾᏝᎥ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏒᎾᏙᏛᏩᏍᏗ ᏱᎩ ᏍᏊ ᏱᏣᎾᏢᎦ ᎡᎵᏅ ᏍᏗ ᎠᏕᎳ ᏱᏣᏝ ᎠᏬᏎᎸ ᏙᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎰᏩ ᎠᏪᎵᏒ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏃᎴ ᏍᎩᏃ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎤᏟ ᏱᎩᏥᏍᏓᏩᏗᏙ ᎨᎲ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ.
segments.translation: A ‘mythical being,’ they said. It lives in the woods. My late grandma, who lived in Missouri when I was a boy, one of her sons, he would be my uncle, he had a strawberry field. And they said to me, “If you go over there, he might hire you. Even if it’s only for a week. So you can have a little money.” And I believed Grandma, I stayed with Grandma, mostly.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏨᎫᎳᏃ ᏬᎦᏁᎸᏛ Ꮓ ᏒᎯᏰ ᎨᎰ ᎠᏗᎰ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎩᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏧᏛᏃᏟᏍᏙ ᎤᎨᏛᎵᏴ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏩᎩᎶᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᎠᏍᎦᏯ ᏳᏍᏓ ᎤᏙᏢᏒ ᎨᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎠᎦᏂᏏᏂᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎤᏝᏅᎥ ᎥᎾ ᎠᎦᏂᏍᏂᏙᎲ ᏣᏗᎲᏛ ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎸ ᏙᏍ yeah ᏙᏛ Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏓ ᎨᎮᎢ ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎾᏛ ᏴᏫ ᎤᏪᏘ ᏣᏃᎮᎰ ᏳᏍᏓ ᎤᏛᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᎦᏛᎦᏅ ᏱᎨᏎ ᎠᏯ. ᎡᎮ ᏛᏙ ᏃᎴ
segments.translation: We moved back to Missouri. She said, “It was late in the evening, something was making noise down in the holler. I went down there, and I saw something that looked like a man that was dragging something around. And he had something in it.” I said, “What was it?” And she said, “It was what they call ‘an ancient man’.” I’ve never heard of that before. They really did exist.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏙᏛᏫᏕᎾ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᎣᎨᏅᏒ Anderson, Missouri ᏣᎾᏗᎰ ᎤᏛᏐᏅ ᏃᏭ ᎣᎩᎾᎵᎪ ᎨᎲ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏙᎩᏂᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏠᎨᏌ ᏐᏈᎵ ᏚᎾᏝᎥ, well ᏫᏓᏥᏴᏅᏛ Ꮎ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎠᏪᎵᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎠᏯᏅ ᎠᎩᏃᎮᏍᎨ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏐᏈᎵ ᏱᏙᏍᏛᎩᎸᏓ ᎠᎪᎮᎴ. Ꮓ ᎥᎾ ᏗᏥᏁᎸ ᏗᏢ ᎾᎠ ᏃᏭ ᎦᎢᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏃᏛ ᏅᏯ ᏕᎦᏥᎯᎰ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᎠᏎᏃ ᎢᎬᏩᏍᏗᏭ ᎦᎢᏐ ᏣᏗᎲ boy ᏃᏫᏛ ᏩᎦᏍᎦᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏓᎥᏩᎪᏢᏒ ᏣᏗᎲ. ᏙᎩ ᎤᏍᏓ ᎤᎵᏍᏛᏁᎢ? ᏅᏱ ᏓᏩᏂᏍᏗᎲ ᎪᎱᏍᏓ ᎤᏛᏅᏅ. ᎠᎩᏄᎸᎲᎦ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᏩᎩᎷᎯᏍᏗᎢ ᎪᎱᏍᏗᏅ ᎤᎦᏎᏍᏗᏕᎦ ᎢᎡᎮᎢ ᎣᎨᎵᏒᏭ.
segments.translation: One Saturday we went to Anderson, Missouri. I was working with an elderly White man. We used to work with him in the fields. He had horses. “I’m going to go get that boy,” he was referring to me, we rode horses sometimes. He was going towards our house, and he said rocks started landing in front of him. He kept on going, but the rocks kept landing in front of him. He said, “I got scared and turned around.” And he said, “I couldn’t make it to y’all’s house.” There was something there that protected our house.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎮᏂ ᏒᏃᏱ ᏲᎦᏂᏢᏂ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏧᏩᏂᏝᎲᏍᎬ ᎦᏍᎩᎸ ᏒᎾᎴᏴ Ꮓ ᎦᏳᎵᏛ ᎤᏑᏩ ᎢᎨᏐ. ᏌᏭ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᎠᎩᏰᏍᏛᏅ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏓᏳᏓᏃᏟᏍᏛ ᏗᏖᎵᏙ ᏃᎴ ᏴᎩ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏛᏳᏃᏴᎬ ᎤᏟᎯ ᏱᎩᏩᏮᏚᏢᏅ. Ꮓ ᏒᎾᎴ ᏄᎵᏍᏛᏂ Ꮓ ᏙᏢ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏯᏝᎮᏃ. ᎯᏅᏅ ᏨᏗᎲ ᏳᏓᎭ ᎢᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎪ ᎪᎱᏍᏗᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏙᎡᎯ ᎠᏎᎾ Ꮲ ᏱᎦᎾᏔ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: When we went to bed at night, they would always put food out, and in the morning, it would be gone. One time the noise woke me up, you could hear the utensils and plates. And then I really covered up and, the next day, there wasn’t anything there. But like you were saying, sometimes I think about it—there really is something out there.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎧᏃᎮᏍᎪ Ꮎ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎮᎾ ᎠᏂᎦᏔᎲ ᏴᏫ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ᎠᏂᎧᎲᏍᎨ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᎦᏎᏍᏓ ᎠᏁᏠᎮᎾ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎠᏗᏍᎪ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᏝᎲᏍᎨ ᎠᎵᏍᏓᏴᏗ. ᏒᎾᎴ Ꮕ ᏱᎩ Ꮲ ᏱᎦᏠ
segments.translation: A long time ago, my dad used to say people knew about things, and they would put something in their house to protect the house. Sometimes they would feed it. They would put food on the table, and it would be gone the next morning.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏅ ᏍᎩᎴ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏯᎦᏔᎭ ᎡᎨᎵᏍᎪ ᎡᎵᏏ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᏂ ᎦᏓᏅᏖᏍᎪ ᏃᎴ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏧᏭᎪᎮ ᏍᏊᎴ ᎥᎾᏝ ᏱᎩᎡᎨᎵᎰ
segments.translation: I used to think that Grandma knew how to do stuff like that. And maybe when she saw that Thing, it was her servant.

segments.speaker: mitch-holcomb
segments.text: ᎠᎦᏘᏯᏛ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎪ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᎦᏘ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎦᏛᎦᏁᎸ
segments.translation: They would call them that Watchman. I’ve heard that, too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᎮᏂ ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎩᏗ
segments.translation: That’s fascinating.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎤᏍᏆᏂᎩᏓᏛ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ
segments.translation: Fascinating things.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎾᎮᏂ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏧᏫᏗᎪᏩᏘᎰ Ꭼ ᏴᏗ ᏳᏍᏓ ᏤᎲ ᎥᎾ ᎢᎾᎨ
segments.translation: When we look out into the woods, we don’t know what all is out there.

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: ᎾᎾ ᏅᏬᏘ ᏣᏂᎦᏔᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎾᏍᏕᏢ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎴᏱᎩ ᎤᏴᎯᏓ ᏍᏓᏅᏛᏗᏍᎪ ᎨᏏ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎣᏩᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏱᎩ Ꮲ
segments.translation: What about for instance—when people used to know about medicine, roots and plants and things like that—do you all remember things like that, like for pain?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎠᎸᎯᏳ ᎮᏂ Ꮟ ᎬᏗᏍᎪ ᎠᏮᏌ ᏩᎩᏲᎰ. ᎾᏅ ᎧᎵᏎᏥ ᏱᎩ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏃᎵᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎸ ᎠᎩᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎮᎾ ᏱᎩᎠᏂᎦᏔᎲ ᏅᏬᏘ ᎪᎱᏍᏗᎡᎾᎨ ᏭᏂᎩᏓ. ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᏯᎩᏃᏎᎰ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎩᏙᏓ ᏍᏊ ᎮᏂ ᎡᏥ ᎠᎩᏃᏎᎸ ᎨᎲ ᎯᎢ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎸᎯᏳ ᏍᏊ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏂᏣᎵᏍᏓᏁᎲᎾ ᏱᎩ ᎠᏬᏎᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏫᏣᏲᎮᏍᏗ ᎯᎦᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᎭᏗᏔᏍᎨᏍᏗ ᎠᏬᏎᎰ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᎾᏃ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ Ꮩ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏛᎸᏱ ᎯᏰᎸ ᎠᎳ ᎤᎶᎯᏍᏗ ᎥᎾᏅ ᏓᎵᏍᏚᎲᏍᎩ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏬᏎᎰ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ Ꮓ ᎧᎵᏎᏥ ᏥᏃᎵᏍᏓᏁ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᏯᏗᏔᏍᎩ ᏱᏓᎵᏍᏚᎢ ᎠᏪᏎᎰ ᎮᏂ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Yeah, I still use it. I go look for it [medicine]. Like for instance for medicine for diabetes—my dad told me about it. They knew a lot of things, back then, to get in the woods. But my dad didn’t usually tell me. It was mostly my mom who told me stuff like this. She used to say, “Even if there isn’t anything wrong with you, go out and get it, boil it, and drink it. You have a whole lot of pores in your body for the sweat to go through, and they get clogged up, and that’s how you get diabetes.” She would say, “And if you drink that, it will open your pores.”

segments.speaker: michael-cooksey
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏯᏅᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏧᏙᎢᏓ ᎨᎲ?
segments.translation: You don’t remember what that was called?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎥᎥ, ᏲᏛ ᎠᏩᏅᏔᏲ ᎠᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎨᎲ. ᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎤᏔᏂ ᎠᏛᏍᎩ ᏱᎩᏴᏫ ᎮᏂ ᏱᎩᏓ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎰ ᎠᏓ ᏗᏓᎶᏂᎨ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏃᏎᎰ ᎮᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏳᎲᎵ ᏙᏫᏍᎬᎨ ᎮᏂ ᎠᏓ ᏃᎴᏍᏊ ᎤᏩᏂᎬᏢ ᏱᏣᏍᏆᎵᏏ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎤᎦᎾᏍᏗ ᎮᏂ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏒᎩ. ᎾᎮᏂᏍᏊ ᎠᎹᏳᏟᏗ ᏗᏛᏍᎦ. ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎣᎩᎦᏁᎰ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮓ ᏥᏓᏴᏝᏗᏍᎪ tea ᎪᏢᏍᎬ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᏣᏗᏔᏍᎪ Ꮲ ᏍᎩᎦ ᎤᏴᏟ ᏱᎦᏲᏂ ᎠᏗᏍᎪ ᎮᏂ
segments.translation: Yeah, I know what that is, it doesn’t grow big but, it’s just about [gestures] high. It was called ‘yellow wood’. It doesn’t have any bark, it’s just smooth. If you break the limb off, and break it, it smells sweet. They grow along the creek. That’s what our dad would brew us when it started to get cold. Dad would make tea, and we would drink that. He would say we wouldn’t catch a cold.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏙᏛ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎠᏂᎦᏔᎾᎡ ᎮᏂ Ꮩ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ. ᏍᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏙᎯ ᎠᏁᎯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.translation: Truly—like you said, they did know some things back then. It seemed like they were healthier back then.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎤᏴᏟ ᎤᏛᎭ ᏦᏂᏱ ᎪᎯᏴ ᏥᎩ ᎦᏲᏟᎨ ᏴᎦᎾᎵ ᎪᏥᎩᎾ ᎩᏔᏯ ᏡᎪ ᏅᎩ ᏗᎦᎲᎸᏗ ᎧᎸᎦ ᏗᏢ ᏩᏁᎢᎾ ᎤᏪᏘᎨ ᏡᎪᏍᏊ ᏅᎩ ᏗᎦᎲᎸᏗ ᏍᎪ ᎧᎸᎦ ᏗᏢ ᏱᏣᎦᏂ ᎥᎾᎦᏠᎢ ᏛᏲ ᎠᏗᏓᏍᎢ ᎢᎦᏗ ᎮᏂ Ᏺ ᎧᎵᏤᏥ ᏍᏗ ᏯᎾᏑᏴᎦ. ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᎩᎦᏁᎲ. ᎠᏮᏌ ᏕᏍᎫ ᏍᎩ ᏯᏮᏁᎸ
segments.translation: Even if you got old. Nowadays, if you weren’t so lazy, you’d peel four pieces of bark from a cherry tree in the direction of the east. And hickory—peel four pieces of bark on the east side, and you brew it. It’s real bitter, some put sugar on it. That’s what they’d brewed us, and I’ve done it myself, too.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᎥᎾᏍᏕᏢ ᏙᎨ Ꮩ?
segments.translation: The root or what?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎲᎥ, ᎤᎲᎸᏭᏅ. ᎧᎸᎬ ᏗᏢ ᏱᏗᏣᎦᎲᎸ ᏅᎩ
segments.translation: No, just the bark. You would peel four pieces [from the side facing] towards the east.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏅᏛᎭ ᎯᎦᏔᎯᏍ Ꮕ ᎬᏃᏒᏍᏗ ᏣᏃᎮᎰ? Ꮕ ᏠᎨᏏᏢ ᎤᎪᏗ. ᎬᏃᏒᏍᏗ ᏛᎮ ᏙᏃᏢᏍᎨ ᎪᎯᎦ. ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎠᏯ ᎥᎩᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏲᎰ ᎨᎮ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎥᎾᏍᏕᏝ ᎠᎦᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏴᏟ flu ᏱᎩ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏥᏃᎵᏍᏓᏁᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏗᏔᏍᎪ ᎠᎵᏟᏗᏍᎬ ᎮᏂ Ꮎ ᎠᏗᏔᏍᎬ
segments.translation: Do you know about the broom plant? It grows in the field a lot. They used to make brooms out of it. My sister used to look for that, and she would brew the roots. If you got the flu or the cold, she drinks that. Boiling it and drinking it.

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᎵ ᏛᎭ Ᏺ ᏲᎴᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏙᎲ
segments.translation: That makes you sweat, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: yeah, ᎠᎵ ᏛᏲ ᏣᎴᏗᎰ
segments.translation: Yeah, it’ll make you sweat.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᏛᎮ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎦᏅᎪᏩᏍᎪ ᏃᏒᎾ ᏙᎲ. ᎯᎾ ᏍᏛᏯᏛᏛᏂ ᎣᏂ ᏗᏢ, ᎯᎾ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎬᏬᏂᎯᏍᏓ ᏤᏙ ᏥᏗᏬᏂ ᎠᏓᏛᏛᎲᏍᎬ ᎨᏒ ᎤᏩᎦᏗᏗᏒ ᏛᏍᎪᎸᏥ ᎢᎨ ᎢᏍᏕᎵᏍᎪ ᎠᎴ ᏫᏛᎵᏍᏆᏚᎨ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᎦᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᏒ ᏍᏕᎵᏍᎪ ᏙᎨ
segments.translation: It takes all that bad stuff out. I’m going to ask you two this towards the end. This Cherokee that’s here, that we speak. This question here asks if you think it will continue or fade away. What do you y’all think? Or do you think the language will end? What do y’all think?

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᏍᏊᏛ ᏛᎵᏍᏆᏗ ᎮᏂ ᎠᎾᏗᏍᎬ ᎾᏅ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ Ꮭ ᏱᏓᏁᏲᎲᏍᎦ ᏍᎩᏃ ᎠᏲᏁᎦ ᎤᏭᎮᏃ ᏩᏂᏬᏂᏍᎪ ᏍᎩᎾᏃ ᎠᏯ ᎮᏂᏲ ᎠᎩᏛᎦᏅ ᏲᏅ ᏛᎵᏒᏂ ᏣᎾᏗ
segments.translation: They say it’s going to run out because they’re not teaching the kids anymore. And the kids are just speaking English. I heard them say it’s going to run out.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.text: ᏅᎾᎭ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏥᏓᎾᏕᎳᏆ ᏥᏓᏁᏲᎲᏍᎦ ᏛᏳᏍᏕᎸᎨ ᎤᏍᎪᎸᏍᏗ ᏂᎨᏒᎾ ᏙᎨ ᏍᏕᎵ ᏂᎯ ᎨᎲ
segments.translation: What about what the teachers are teaching here? Do y’all think they’re keeping it from fading?

segments.speaker: jerry-cochran
segments.text: ᎠᎾᏕᎳᏆᏛ ᏴᏗᎾᏗ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᎠᏎᎾ ᏧᎾᏓᎬᏴᎵᎨᎾ ᎤᎬᏫᏳ. Ꮭ ᎠᏣᎳᎩ ᏳᎾᏂᎩᏌ ᏅᏃ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏙᏧᏃᏝ ᏚᎾᏓᎬᏴᎵᎨ ᏗᏗᏴᎵᏔᏍᎦ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏧᎾᏝᏃᎮᏗ ᏲᏁᎦ ᏍᎩᎮᏂ ᎢᎩᏍᎦᏅᏍᎩ ᏔᎵᏅ ᏍᏊᎤᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎯᎢ ᎠᏯ ᏥᏗᏬᏂ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎾᎮᏂ ᏧᎾᏕᎳᏆᎥᏭ ᏥᏓᏅᏕᏲᎲᏍᎩ ᎮᏍᏗᎮᏂ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎾᏂᏪ
segments.translation: They’re learning while they’re little, but their parents don’t speak Cherokee. And then the TV is in English, and the phones are in English. That’s what’s working against us. How they’re teaching them is probably not the right way to teach things. The teachers that are teaching are second language learners, and that’s why the ones learning and teaching aren’t saying it good.

segments.speaker: henry-sawney
segments.text: ᎮᏍᏗᎧ ᎧᎵ ᏱᎩ ᏳᏍᏗ
